#5089. RLUSD supply grew 30% on Ethereum and fell 20% on XRPL – Assessing…

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

RLUSD is growing while USDT and USDC are losing supply.

At the macro level, the stablecoin sector is in a relatively weak phase. In Q4 alone, the market lost over $20 billion of value. As a result, the overall stablecoin market cap has fallen below $300 billion.

This means that all of the market’s growth since Q3 2025 (when it peaked at above $320 billion) has been erased. Notably, USDT and USDC account for more than half of the total liquidity outflows during this period.

In contrast, RLUSD has increased by almost 20% during this period. This represents an increase of almost $500 million in total supply, pushing its total market cap to a record $2.9 billion.

In essence, RLUSD is attracting fresh liquidity even as the broader stablecoin market continues to contract.

This raises an important question: Which L1 stands to benefit the most from this growth?

Fundamentally, Ethereum supports much larger amounts of RLUSD in comparison to XRPL, with 72%+ of RLUSD ($2.08 billion) on Ethereum. In addition, supply growth on Ethereum is relatively higher.

In the last 30 days, RLUSD supply has increased by 30% on Ethereum, whereas supply has fallen by 20% on XRPL.

So, with RLUSD liquidity increasingly concentrated on Ethereum even as the broader stablecoin market faces outflows, Ethereum seems to be the clear winner. However, supply is only one side of the story, and XRPL’s transaction volume shows why it should not be overlooked.

Growing stablecoin supply and actually using that supply are two different things.

Interestingly, this difference is becoming important in comparing Ethereum [ETH] and XRPL’s on-chain activity around RLUSD. On-chain data shows that nearly $11.716 billion worth of RLUSD was transacted on the XRP Ledger and Ethereum in the week up to the 1st of November 2026.

The key takeaway? XRPL handled the larger share of RLUSD activity. As the chart below shows, $6.699 billion was transacted on the XRPL network, representing 57% of the total RLUSD volume. The Ethereum blockchain had total transactions of $5.017 billion (42.82%).

So, although there is more RLUSD on the Ethereum blockchain, XRPL is seeing higher transaction volume.

Notably, RLUSD’s DEX activity on XRPL is also picking up.

The total DEX volume reached an all-time high of $596.2 million in the week ending August. While volume has dropped in recent weeks, it has been consistently above $70 million per week for the last 10 weeks.

More recently, volume has picked up again, exceeding $200 million per week. This is significantly higher than previous averages of approximately $15 million.

So, while there is more RLUSD on Ethereum, XRPL is seeing higher transaction volume and growing DEX activity. This suggests that more RLUSD is being used on XRPL, making it a network to watch as the stablecoin continues to grow.

RLUSD supply is growing despite broader stablecoin outflows, with Ethereum holding over 72% of its total supply.

XRPL handles 57% of RLUSD transaction volume and is seeing a sharp rise in DEX activity.

Shiba Inu (SHIB) community members have launched a new block explorer for Shibarium, the layer-2 network of the SHIB ecosystem, and Shiba Inu lead Shytoshi Kusama has remained silent on X since May.

Shiba Inu community veteran Mazrael announced the new explorer, scan.shibfun.app, in an X post. "Shibarium has a new block explorer," he wrote. According to Mazrael, the explorer was "built by the community, powered by ShibWatch, dressed in the Eternity Hub look."

The launch comes as SHIB trades near its lowest levels in years. In November, the price of SHIB fell as low as $0.00000337, its lowest level since 2021, and on Nov. 22, the token traded at around $0.00000362, according to CoinMarketCap.

According to the post, users can type a .shib name in the search bar and land on the wallet linked to it, and the explorer also shows new Shiboshis from Shibarium every day. For developers, Mazrael listed contract verification, read and write functions for contracts, the activity of ERC-4337 smart wallets, and a free API, which he described as "Etherscan-style too." Method names are decoded as well, and in Mazrael's words, there are "no more mystery 0x codes." The explorer also has a DApps page with Shibarium games and apps, and a button that adds Shibarium to a wallet in one click.

The work on the explorer is not finished yet. "Live blocks are complete now, and older history indexing," Mazrael wrote. On Tuesday, the explorer itself showed that 3% of Shibarium blocks had been indexed, and a notice on the site said that some of the counts may be inaccurate. Mazrael added that the new explorer can be found on Shib.io under ShibWatch.

Shytoshi Kusama's last post or interaction on X dates back to May 13, 2026. In September, Kusama changed his X bio to "Polish" and his location to "Close," and he has not explained the meaning of either word. The official Shibarium account on X has not posted since July 13, 2026.

Still, Shibarium updates kept coming from community members. In October, Mazrael said that CreateX, a standard factory for deploying contracts at the same address on different chains, went live on Shibarium. According to Mazrael, all 12 Safe v1.4.1 contracts were deployed to their canonical addresses through the Safe Singleton Factory, and x402 went live too, so AI agents can now pay in SHIB, TREAT and wrapped BONE.

In September 2025, attackers exploited the Shibarium bridge and withdrew about $2.4 million worth of assets from it.

According to Shibariumscan, Shibarium processed 546 transactions in a single day in late November, and on Oct. 31, the daily number of transactions on the network was 6,370. Since its launch in August 2023, Shibarium has processed more than 1.5 billion transactions in total.

At the same time, the number of SHIB holders on Ethereum passed 1.7 million on Nov. 17, according to Etherscan.

However, convenience comes with a catch. Not all crypto exchanges accept credit cards, some banks block crypto transactions outright, and high “cash advance” fees can silently eat into your investment if you don’t know what to look for.

Whether you are making your very first crypto purchase or simply want the quickest checkout method available, this step-by-step guide walks you through the exact process, breaks down the real costs, and shows you how to avoid rookie mistakes.

Once you pick a platform, sign up using your email address and create a strong, unique password. Immediately enable Two-Factor Authentication using an authenticator app (like Google Authenticator) rather than SMS text messages, which are vulnerable to SIM-swap attacks.

Most major exchanges automate this process, approving your account within 2 to 5 minutes.

Navigate to your account’s Payment Methods or Billing settings and select Add a Credit/Debit Card. Enter your 16-digit card number, expiration date, CVV security code, and billing address.

Pro tip: Make sure the billing address on your exchange account matches your credit card statement word-for-word. Even a minor mismatch will trigger an automatic fraud decline.

Head to the Buy Crypto section, select Bitcoin (BTC) as the asset you want to receive, and choose your linked credit card as the payment method.

Enter the amount you want to spend in your local currency (e.g., $100 or €100). Before hitting confirm, pause on the order preview screen and check two numbers:

Once you confirm the order, the exchange charges your card and credits your Bitcoin balance immediately.

Congratulations—you officially own Bitcoin! Right now, your BTC is sitting in your exchange’s custodial wallet. If you only bought a small amount (50–200) to get started, leaving it on a major, regulated exchange is fine while you learn the ropes.

However, if you plan to hold significant value long-term, transfer your Bitcoin to a self-custody wallet (such as a Ledger or Trezor hardware wallet, or a reputable mobile wallet like BlueWallet).

In crypto, holding your own private keys ensures that nobody—not even the exchange—can freeze or lose your funds.

The Golden Rule: Never buy Bitcoin on credit if you cannot pay off the card balance in full before your next billing cycle. Paying 25% interest on a volatile asset is a quick way to lose money even if Bitcoin’s price goes up.

#5085. GTA 6 Leaker Dangles a PC Port Behind a $15 Million Crypto Pump

GTA 6 Leaker Dangles a PC Port Behind a $15 Million Crypto Pump

A notorious Grand Theft Auto 6 leaker is holding a potential PC version of the game hostage to a cryptocurrency payday, promising to release the final file needed to make a leaked build playable once its meme coin hits a $15 million market cap.

The leaker, who goes by Cyberleek, has released what it claims is a near-complete 209 GB Xbox build of GTA 6 from November 2026 via torrent, according to a report from PC Gamer.

The one piece withheld is the main executable, the file that would let modders begin emulating the game on PC, potentially bringing it to the platform long before Rockstar Games intends.

You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Bitcoin with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.

Here’s the crypto catch. Cyberleek says it will release the executable on Nov. 23 regardless, but will drop it early if its token, called CYBERLEEK, reaches a $15 million market cap. That’s half the $30 million target the leaker floated in October.

The pressure tactic doesn’t appear to be working: the token is trading around $0.002 as of the weekend, with a market cap of roughly $1.3 million, more than $13 million short of the goal. The coin is down some 20% on the week, but the numbers will fluctuate wildly given the very thin liquidity on a small cap coin.

The setup has drawn open skepticism that it’s a cash grab, or worse. Observers have warned it could be an attempt to pump the coin before a rug pull, the crypto term for abandoning a token after luring buyers in. Cyberleek has also claimed to hold a PS5 build as a fallback if the Xbox files can’t be made to work.

The episode sits at the increasingly busy intersection of crypto, piracy, and AI. Modern Xbox games are architecturally closer to PC software than PlayStation titles, and AI coding tools have accelerated the kind of decompilation work that makes fast ports plausible, the same dynamic behind a wave of AI-assisted game ports this year.

It also caps a chaotic launch window for GTA that crypto has repeatedly crashed. One trader banked around $66,000 on a GTA 6 meme coin amid ticker confusion, and the game’s disc-free, digital-only release has fueled broader debate, with GameStop’s CEO arguing that digital-only games have hurt consumers.

None of the leaked files have been independently confirmed as genuine, and there is still no official GTA 6 PC version; Rockstar, famously litigious, could respond with legal action rather than a port.

Mutsamudu, Comoros, November 24, 2026 – MEXC, a pioneer in 0-fee digital asset trading, has released its September–October 2026 security report. The report shows that the MEXC Guardian Fund increased its BTC holdings to 2,000 BTC, while reserve ratios for four major assets—BTC, ETH, USDT, and USDC—remained above 100%.

The crypto industry faces security challenges across multiple points of exposure. The report recorded 196 security incidents in September–October, with total asset losses exceeding $7.3 billion. Several large-scale incidents involved breaches of exchange wallets and transaction signing systems that enabled unauthorized asset transfers. Attackers used fake recruitment campaigns to persuade employees to download malware, exploited vulnerabilities in third-party tools to steal internal credentials, and distributed phishing links through compromised official accounts. These incidents have drawn greater attention to platforms’ access controls and reserve transparency.

In September 2026, MEXC allocated an additional 1,000 BTC to the Guardian Fund, marking its second addition of the year. By the end of September, the fund held 2,000 BTC and more than 100 million USDT, maintaining reserves in both BTC and USDT.

The Guardian Fund is designed to support user protection in serious security incidents, including major exploits, targeted attacks, and unforeseen system vulnerabilities. The latest addition follows MEXC’s plan, announced in May 2026, to expand the fund to $500 million within two years. MEXC has published the fund’s holding addresses so users can review on-chain balances and transaction records:

MEXC’s October 9, 2026 reserve snapshot showed reserve ratios above 100% for all four major assets disclosed. The BTC reserve ratio stood at 293.86%, with wallet assets of 12,402.93 BTC against user assets of 4,220.56 BTC. The ETH reserve ratio was 110.90%, with wallet assets of 59,691.16 ETH against user assets of 53,820.65 ETH. USDT and USDC reserve ratios were 122.38% and 115.42%, respectively.

Users can review platform wallet and user asset data on the MEXC Proof of Reserves and Asset Protection page and use Merkle tree verification to check whether their account balances are included in that reserve snapshot.

As of November 5, 2026, the MEXC Futures Insurance Fund held 830,411,315 USDT. This was an increase of 38,714,893 USDT, or 4.89%, from the September 1 balance disclosed in the previous report.

The Futures Insurance Fund covers deficits caused by insufficient margin during forced liquidation. It provides a financial buffer during sharp market swings and helps reduce the risk of triggering auto-deleveraging (ADL). Users can view the fund balance and historical changes on the MEXC Trust page.

MEXC helps users recover assets deposited in error. In September–October, its customer service team manually completed 1,354 returns of erroneous deposits, returning assets worth 1,002,660 USDT. Compared with July–August, the number of completed returns increased 65.5%, while the value of assets returned rose 66.5%.

MEXC CEO Vugar Usi said, “In the AI era, attackers can find vulnerabilities and develop attacks faster. Exchanges must also upgrade their technical defenses, strengthen internal controls, and improve their incident response capabilities. MEXC will continue to invest in security, build up its protection reserves, and regularly report on progress in user protection. Through sustained security investment and transparent disclosure, we aim to build lasting trust with our users.”

Founded in 2018, MEXC is a leading global multi-asset trading platform built as your 0-fee gateway to infinite opportunities. Serving users across 170+ markets, MEXC provides simple and efficient access to crypto, stocks, tokenized assets, derivatives, and a growing range of TradFi-linked opportunities through one account and one gateway.

With 0 trading fees, deep liquidity, broad asset coverage, and a high-performance trading experience, MEXC is designed for retail users who want to discover earlier, act faster, and trade with fewer barriers. #5082. Flop Labs Pushes Back Testnet Launch Amid Final Preparations

Flop Labs has announced a minor delay to the launch of its public testnet, pushing back from its previous goal of 15:00 (UTC+8) on November 24.

It's unclear what the reason for the delay is, although the team does expect to launch the testnet before 18:00 (UTC+8) the same day.

Possible reasons for the delay could include conducting final checks, calibrating nodes, validator onboarding, load testing, etc. (although Flop Labs has not confirmed any of these to be the reason for the delay).

It does not appear that Flop Labs has any plans to move the testnet launch to another day.

Flop Labs is building FLOP Network, a blockchain serving as a settlement layer for what it calls the "agentic economy". This would enable AI agents to make payments for computation (e.g. model inference) and memory services, and provide rewards to GPU miners that contribute their computational power to fulfill these requests.

Computation is verified via Flop Labs' "Proof of Useful Inference", which entails miners providing evidence that they've carried out the desired AI computation, and validators checking this evidence.

Why does this matter? FLOP Network would enable agents to make payments for computation, memory, etc. Flop Labs' main competitors include Akash Network and io.net (both of which facilitate access to compute/gpu resources in a decentralized manner), as well as Render Network (which started out facilitating decentralized graphics rendering but has since expanded into AI/compute more broadly).

While Flop Labs' competitors also facilitate access to compute, Flop Labs' main differentiating factor appears to be its focus on facilitating agent-to-agent commerce and computation-verification.

Flop Labs is led by Arthur Hayes, co-founder of crypto exchange BitMEX and current chief investment officer at Maelstrom. The rest of Flop Labs' team includes Sergey Vidyuk (ex-Deutsche Bank/BitMEX) as CTO, and Shu Duan (with experience in investment banking and crypto asset management) as chief strategy officer.

The testnet would be an opportunity to see if Flop Labs can successfully build out its envisioned agentic economy.

Google's Quantum Chip Beats Classical Limits in 'Impossible' Game

Google says its Willow quantum processor won a mathematical coordination game 98.3% of the time, above the 88.9% maximum attainable by classical strategies, in a Science study published Thursday.

The experiment tests quantum contextuality, so measurement outcomes depend on what else is measured alongside them. Google researchers explained that “you cannot assign fixed, pre-existing values to everything you might measure.”

Don’t panic. The result does not mean Google has a commercial quantum computer, nor that its largest experiment beat every classical machine. The 98.3% figure came from four qubits—the basic unit of information used to encode data in quantum computing—the 105-qubit run tested a different, more limited challenge.

You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Google with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.

The first test used the Mermin-Peres magic square game, which asks two players to fill intersecting parts of a three-by-three grid without communicating. Their answers must obey conflicting row-and-column rules and match at the shared square.

A prearranged classical strategy can succeed on no more than eight of nine assignments, or 88.9%. Entangled qubits can theoretically win every round, while Google’s physical processor won 98.3% across 900,000 trials, according to the researchers.

The researchers wrote that “our qubits coordinated better than any pre-written table allows.” Unavoidable hardware noise prevented the result from reaching the quantum ideal.

Google also measured contextuality. Any model with predetermined outcomes scores at most 4; quantum theory allows 6. Willow registered 5.590, with a reported uncertainty of 0.008.

A separate GHZ parity game asked up to 71 entangled qubits to deliver coordinated binary answers. Success was measured against the strongest classical winning rate, which approaches 50% with more players; Google remained above that limit throughout its tests, despite accumulating hardware noise.

Researchers also verified genuine entanglement across 45 qubits. In the hidden linear function task, a shallow quantum circuit had to produce a binary string satisfying mathematical constraints. The processor reached roughly 60% success using 105 qubits.

Google says the tasks exposed small, systematic errors that conventional randomized tests can hide. Its corporate blog called contextuality testing “a sensitive new method to catch subtle hardware errors,” potentially helping engineers evaluate circuits used for chemistry and materials research.

The work follows Google's October report of a 40-fold error reduction in preparing magic states, a resource needed for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

For Bitcoin, the looming danger is that a future fault-tolerant quantum computer could break digital signatures, but that is still far from happening. Google’s 105-qubit task was instead a shallow mathematical circuit, and its largest instance still failed in about four out of 10 runs.

The past 24 hours have delivered a reality check to investors.

Following weeks of selling due to the Jensen Huang situation, around $8 trillion was wiped off the U.S. stock market. However, on the 23rd of November, following the re-appointment of the CEO, almost $3 trillion flowed back almost immediately. NVDA soared by more than 31% and gained back two weeks’ worth of value in one day, showing how quickly sentiment can shift when uncertainty fades.

However, the same recovery did not spill over into crypto. Ethereum initially rose above $1,800 only for it to then trend back down to around the $1,700 mark by the close. The key takeaway? Capital is returning to stocks, but crypto is struggling to attract the same demand. This growing divergence has put “ETH vs. NVDA” at the center of a new debate over where investors see better opportunities.

Interestingly, investors are using five-year returns to make their case.

One post pointed out that investing $10,000 in ETH 5 years ago would now be worth approximately $4,200, marking a 58% loss. This pales in comparison to the over $12,500 that the same investment in NVDA would now be worth, delivering a 25% gain. That’s an $8,300 gap in return on the same investment, adding to the debate over whether investors now see better opportunities in stocks than in crypto.

In this context, the past 24 hours have delivered a reality check for investors. This raises a key question: Is the ongoing ETH distribution  indicative of this change in long-term ownership as money flows once again into stocks? And could this put further pressure on Ethereum [ETH] and ETH-heavy treasury firms?

The past 24 hours have brought some much-needed relief for digital asset treasuries.

It appears that the current NVDA outperformance is boosting sentiment in the U.S. stock market generally, with almost $3 trillion re-entering. In crypto too, several treasury stocks are benefiting. BitMine, for example, has surged by over 11% and recorded its best weekly inflow in more than 3 months. This suggests that improving sentiment could also be supporting demand for ETH-focused companies.

However, Ethereum’s spot flows tell a different story. As shown below, a whale sent a further 85,500 ETH (around $146.98 million) to Binance. Over the past seven days, the same whale has deposited 176,000 ETH (worth approximately $309.21 million) into the exchange. Furthermore, institutional sentiment continues to be negative. BlackRock has seen net withdrawals of 1 million+ ETH, valued at $1.75 billion since October.

This creates a clear divergence: ETH-focused stocks are recovering, while spot market flows continue to signal selling pressure.

That shifts the focus back to the Ethereum vs. Nvidia debate. While treasury stocks are recovering, whales continue to sell, and institutions are also exiting. This suggests that there is still weak demand for spot crypto. Investors seem to be moving away from crypto and into equities.

If this trend continues, it could suggest a broader change in the long-term holding strategy of investors. Whales may not just be selling ETH at random but could be actively moving funds out of the asset and into equities such as NVDA.

NVDA is gaining, but Ethereum is still struggling to attract buyers.

Whale selling could signal a shift from ETH to stocks like NVDA.

#5079. Bitcoin Loses $60,000 And Gold Offers No Protection During Its Worst Selloff Since 1982

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

The Bitcoin price fell back below $60,000 on Tuesday, cutting short a recovery that had taken the cryptocurrency above $64,000 a day earlier. But perhaps the more troubling development for investors is happening outside the crypto market.

Gold is going through a severe correction of its own, leaving investors in two assets often associated with wealth preservation facing substantial losses.

This is not the first time Bitcoin and gold have struggled simultaneously. What makes the current environment particularly difficult is that neither asset generates income at a time when interest-bearing investments offer an increasingly attractive alternative.

The question is no longer simply whether Bitcoin is digital gold. It is whether investors have enough reason to own either asset under current monetary conditions.

The selling extended well beyond Bitcoin. Figures from the World Gold Council show that Bitcoin lost 13.7%, gold fell 8.3% and the Nasdaq dropped 10%, while the US Dollar Index gained 0.4%. The numbers point to a broader reduction in risk exposure rather than a selloff specific to crypto.

Gold declined 24.6% over the 60 days ending November 23, its steepest loss over such a period since 1982.

The World Gold Council’s latest market assessment, published on Monday, identified several risks facing the precious metal, including pressure on leveraged equity and credit positions, restrictive monetary policy and the possibility of another disappointing US inflation report.

The organization also identified the lack of a clear reduction in speculative positioning as a concern.

This matters for Bitcoin because the argument for buying BTC during a gold correction often assumes that capital leaving one scarce asset will eventually find its way into the other.

There is little reason to assume that happens automatically.

An investor selling gold to reduce leverage or meet a margin requirement is unlikely to replace that exposure immediately with Bitcoin. The priority is raising cash, not finding another store of value.

There is also a difference between selling an asset because its investment thesis has deteriorated and selling because the cost of maintaining a position has become too expensive. The latter can create opportunities for patient buyers, but it rarely provides a reliable indication of when a market will bottom.

Monday’s trading session offered Bitcoin investors some encouragement. The cryptocurrency recovered above $64,000 following the previous week’s decline to its lowest levels in roughly two years.

The broader picture is hardly encouraging. Bitcoin has lost nearly 24% over the past three months, falling from a period high of $86,578 to a low of $58,178. Although BTC has since recovered above $60,000, the bounce has done little to change the broader downward trend.

Tuesday’s return below $60,000 raises questions about the strength of the recovery, particularly given the improvement in technology stocks during Monday’s session.

If Bitcoin struggles to sustain gains when conditions improve elsewhere, investors should be careful about assuming that another equity market rally will necessarily pull BTC higher.

There is also an important distinction between a recovery driven by fresh buyers and one driven by traders closing profitable short positions. Both can produce impressive green candles. Only the former demonstrates that investors are willing to commit new capital at higher prices.

Spot trading activity, ETF subscriptions and derivatives positioning will offer a better indication of which type of recovery the market is experiencing.

For now, the failure to retain Monday’s gains makes the rebound less convincing than its initial size suggested.

Bitcoin’s recent performance will inevitably revive criticism of its role as a store of value. However, gold’s own losses make that argument considerably less straightforward.

The metal has been used to preserve wealth for centuries, yet it remains vulnerable to changes in interest rates, investor positioning and the strength of the US dollar.

Bitcoin shares some of those vulnerabilities while carrying considerably different market risks, including its dependence on speculative demand and the availability of leverage across cryptocurrency exchanges.

That does not invalidate Bitcoin’s scarcity argument. Its supply characteristics have not changed because its market price has fallen.

What the current correction does challenge is the assumption that scarcity alone guarantees protection during financial stress.

An asset can have a credible long-term investment case and still be a poor short-term hedge. Bitcoin investors would benefit from separating those two propositions rather than defending both every time the market declines.

The immediate focus now turns to Wednesday’s US inflation release.

The Bureau of Economic Analysis is scheduled to publish its October personal consumption expenditures (PCE) report on November 25. The previous release showed annual headline PCE inflation of 3.6%, with core inflation at 3.1%.

Another stronger-than-expected reading could reinforce expectations of restrictive monetary policy, making conditions more difficult for assets that rely heavily on capital appreciation.

A softer reading, particularly if accompanied by falling Treasury yields, could offer some relief to both Bitcoin and gold.

For Bitcoin, however, recovering $60,000 should be treated as a starting point rather than confirmation of a broader reversal. Monday’s trading high above $64,000 represents a more demanding test of whether buyers are prepared to return.

Until that happens, the market has demonstrated that it can bounce. It has yet to demonstrate that it can sustain a recovery.

#5078. Trezor Tells Crypto Users Never to Enter Wallet Backups on Phones Amid Theft Probe

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Crypto wallet provider Trezor has issued a security warning to cryptocurrency users following a recent theft report: "Never type your wallet backup into a phone, app or website."

According to Onchain Lens, a user reported losing over $600,000 across TRON and Solana while using an iPhone 17 Pro Max running iOS 27.2.1. Both the Trezor Safe 7 and the Exodus wallet were reportedly affected. The victim had been using a Trezor Safe 7 for nearly two months.

According to the victim, the Trezor wallet arrived sealed, with no visible tampering; the recovery phrase was generated on the Trezor screen and not on the iPhone; the seed was written on paper and never stored digitally. The victim used Trezor Suite on an iPhone 17 Pro Max via Bluetooth and also had the Exodus wallet on the same iPhone.

The device was running iOS 27.2.1, and the victim never approved the unauthorized transactions. The Trezor wallets for TRON and Solana shared one recovery phrase.

The user said $580,000 was stolen from Trezor on TRON and that an unauthorized transaction moved 49,999 USDT on Nov. 21, 2026. The transaction used the default owner permission, making the signing authority central to the investigation.

Another $23,400 was drained from Trezor on Solana, and the victim says they never approved that transfer using the hardware device. The iPhone remains the main focus, as both Trezor Suite and Exodus were reportedly used on the same iPhone 17 Pro Max running iOS 27.2.1, and both were affected.

Trezor is designed to keep private keys inside the hardware device. However, compromising the phone alone should not normally provide access to Trezor's private keys, and the mechanism behind both thefts remains largely unknown.

On November 9, 2026, Apple issued iOS 27.2.1, which patched several security holes (including some related to Bluetooth). The victim was reportedly running this version when the theft occurred. Thus, there is currently no evidence connecting those vulnerabilities to these transactions. Possible causes outlined included compromised recovery credentials, unauthorized signing, or a device or software security failure.

Trezor responded to this disclosure, saying that Trezor wallets don’t get drained out of nowhere and that there are currently no reports of funds being stolen remotely from any device. It noted that similar cases usually trace back to a compromised wallet backup.

@OnchainLens @binance @Bybit_Official UPDATE: This device came directly from Trezor and shows no sign of an implant. We’re still investigating what happened. So far there’s no confirmed loss of funds from implants and no implant found in any Trezor Safe 7. Never type your wallet backup into a phone, app or website.

In a further update, Trezor confirmed that the device affected came directly from the company and showed no sign of an implant. The wallet provider added that it continues to investigate what happened.

This appears to be a standalone case, as Trezor reiterated that, so far, no confirmed loss of funds from implants has been reported, and no implant has been found in any Trezor Safe 7. It also reiterated an important security warning: users should never enter their wallet backups into a phone, application, or website.

#5077. XRP Hit 29 Cents in Kraken’s Canadian Market Sell-Off

Home » Trendsetter News » XRP Hit 29 Cents in Kraken’s Canadian Market Sell-Off

XRP traded at just 29 cents in Kraken’s Canadian-dollar market during a localized sell-off, raising questions about thin liquidity.

XRP reportedly traded at just 29 cents in Kraken’s Canadian-dollar market during a sharp, localized sell-off discussed by crypto commentator Crypto Sensei.

His video examines whether the trades reflected an exchange-specific liquidity problem rather than a broader XRP collapse, alongside falling ledger activity and disputed price forecasts.

According to the account presented in the video, 11 Canadian-dollar markets fell by at least 65%, with bitcoin trading below 18,000 and ether around 560.

The host cites November 20, 2026 as the incident date and reports that Kraken considered the orders correctly processed and would let the trades stand.

The analyst didn’t include trade records or Kraken’s full statement. Those limits matter: the reported 29-cent execution should not be confused with XRP’s prevailing price across exchanges.

Crypto Sensei attributes the dislocation to heavy selling meeting insufficient liquidity. Buyers may have secured steep discounts, while sellers received prices far below those available elsewhere.

“Whoever sold and just got totally wiped out here, I feel for you,” he says. The video does not establish whether individual losses resulted from discretionary sales, automated orders or liquidations.

A separate headline claiming the XRP Ledger had lost 60% of its users also draws scrutiny.

The underlying figure, according to the clarification cited in the YouTube video, was roughly a 63% decline in daily activity, not evidence that a comparable share of holders permanently departed or sold their XRP.

The host challenges Jake Claver’s repeated $100 year-end XRP forecast, arguing that institutional adoption is a longer process than such targets suggest. He also distinguishes Ripple’s business expansion from confirmed institutional use of XRP itself.

Former Ripple executive and Evernorth CEO Ashish Birla offers a longer-term XRP development case in a clip: Evernorth intends to deploy XRP on-chain, pursue yield and support ecosystem features rather than simply hold the asset. The video leaves the execution details and eventual returns unresolved.

For HODLers, these are separate questions: whether an exchange has enough liquidity, whether ledger usage is growing, and whether adoption creates demand for XRP. A dramatic trade print, or an ambitious treasury strategy, does not answer all three.

#5076. BlackRock Launches Hong Kong Tokenized Fund With A HK$10 Entry Point

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

BlackRock has launched its first tokenized money market fund in Asia-Pacific, giving investors in Hong Kong a new way to move money between traditional investments and blockchain-based financial products.

The BlackRock tokenized fund, known formally as the HKD Digital Liquidity Fund, supports both conventional and tokenized investment units. It also introduces a use case for HKDAP, the Hong Kong dollar stablecoin issued by Standard Chartered-led Anchorpoint Financial.

The development follows Anchorpoint’s plans to expand HKDAP to Solana, announced in late October.

However, there is an interesting detail in BlackRock’s product disclosures. One of the fund’s tokenized classes requires a minimum investment of just HK$10, while access through stablecoins is reportedly limited to professional investors.

The technology may be making financial products more accessible, but the institutions behind them still decide who gets through the door.

BlackRock announced regulatory authorization for the fund on September 10, with its product listings identifying November 16 as the inception date. The commercial launch was reported on Tuesday, November 24.

Unlike many of the investment products available across decentralized finance, BlackRock’s fund does not depend on cryptocurrency lending, liquidity pools or token incentives to generate returns.

Its investment strategy revolves around short-term financial instruments, including government-backed securities and bank deposits.

Investors gain exposure to those assets through fund units. With tokenized units, blockchain technology is used to maintain ownership records.

BlackRock’s official product disclosure lists a minimum initial investment of HK$10 for its D OnChain class, alongside a management fee of 0.31% and daily income distributions.

For comparison, the fund’s conventional I class requires a minimum initial investment of HK$10 million.

The difference is substantial, although a lower investment minimum should not be confused with unrestricted access. Different share classes and distribution channels come with their own conditions.

Perhaps the most interesting part of BlackRock’s launch is what it means for HKDAP.

Anchorpoint Financial, a joint venture between Standard Chartered, Animoca Brands and HKT, received its stablecoin issuer licence from the Hong Kong Monetary Authority in April.

Until now, much of the discussion surrounding regulated Hong Kong dollar stablecoins has focused on payments, transfers and their potential role in financial infrastructure.

BlackRock’s fund introduces another practical application. Eligible investors can use digital money denominated in Hong Kong dollars to access investments denominated in the same currency.

In its September announcement, BlackRock stated:

Imagine a company that already holds HKDAP for operational payments. Instead of leaving all its surplus liquidity in stablecoins, it could potentially move some of that balance into a money market fund and earn investment income while the money is not needed.

The important distinction is that the stablecoin itself is not generating the fund’s returns. The underlying financial instruments are.

For stablecoin issuers, this kind of integration could ultimately prove more valuable than simply securing another exchange listing. It gives businesses a reason to hold and use digital cash beyond cryptocurrency trading.

There is still a noticeable difference between what blockchain infrastructure can do and what BlackRock’s product currently offers.

The D OnChain class lists a daily dealing schedule with an 11 AM Hong Kong time trading deadline and settlement on the trade date.

Anyone familiar with decentralized finance will recognize the contrast. A blockchain does not stop processing transactions because a bank has closed or a fund has passed its dealing deadline.

But tokenizing an investment does not automatically change the operating hours, liquidity arrangements or legal obligations of the underlying fund.

BlackRock also warns that technology failures, compromised wallets and disruptions involving blockchain service providers could interfere with investors’ ability to access or redeem their holdings.

Restrictions on redemptions are possible under stressed market conditions, while investors remain exposed to potential capital losses.

These limitations are not necessarily a failure of tokenization. Institutional investors have regulatory, custody and accounting obligations that cannot simply be removed by deploying a smart contract.

Still, if investors ultimately have to work around many of the same deadlines and intermediaries they encounter in traditional finance, the immediate advantages of tokenization become narrower.

Earlier this month, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority expanded its EnsembleTX settlement initiative to support continuous settlement using tokenized central bank money.

The initiative involves several major financial institutions, including BlackRock, and supports applications involving tokenized deposits and investment funds.

These developments are gradually connecting different parts of the financial system that previously operated separately.

There are now regulated digital currencies, tokenized investment products and settlement infrastructure being developed to move value between them.

However, BlackRock’s latest launch also shows why the size of the tokenization market should not be measured solely by the number of financial products being brought onto blockchains.

The more interesting figures will be how much money actually enters these funds through digital cash, how frequently investors move between the two products and whether those transactions become cheaper or faster.

BlackRock’s product disclosures reviewed for this article did not yet provide usable figures for total fund assets or current yields.

Nor does the launch establish unrestricted access through decentralized exchanges or lending protocols.

Those are the developments worth watching before declaring that tokenized finance has moved beyond institutional adoption and into the hands of ordinary crypto users.

Hong Kong now has another piece of the infrastructure. The next challenge is getting people to use it.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

The Monday New York trading session open brought a flurry of volatility to Bitcoin [BTC] and the rest of the market. Nvidia’s stock soared 31% after the company’s board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, effective immediately.

Combined with the oversold market conditions, the tech and AI-sector stock market bounce helped Bitcoin rally to a local high of $64,603.

Unfortunately for the bulls, the entirety of Monday’s rally has been undone.

At the time of writing, BTC was back below the $61,000 mark. Its rally liquidated $520.89 million in short positions across the crypto market, including $225.58 million for Bitcoin alone.

The BTC spot ETF flows on Monday measured -$60.4 million, extending the bearish market sentiment and highlighting the lack of demand.

The MVRV Z-score measures the difference between market capitalization and realized capitalization. It displayed a reading of 0.24 and has fallen by 0.11 over the past week, reaching among the lowest in four years.

It has remained positive for 1,410 days, reported crypto analyst Axel Adler Jr. A drop below zero would mean that the market cap has fallen below realized cap, a sign of deep capitulation.

Another metric that reached some of its lowest levels in four years was the supply in profit. It compares the market price with the last moved price of coins in the circulating supply.

Less than half of the coins are in profit, mirroring the lows from the previous bear market lows of late 2022.

In August, the cumulative volume delta (CVD) on Binance peaked at +2.41b. This peak showed heavy market buying as prices climbed toward $80k. Yet, as the price pushed to the local high at $87k, the CVD on Binance declined to -6b.

This was a bearish divergence; rising sell market orders captured take-profit behavior, while late entrants and leverage hunts pushed prices higher.

In November, across all exchanges, the CVD’s decline accelerated alongside price drawdown, and Binance’s CVD figure reached -21b, wrote crypto analyst FundingVest.

If the falling CVD momentum slows down while Bitcoin’s price continues its descent, it could be a constructive sign that will considerably increase the chances of a recovery.

#5074. Solana Validators Can Now Stop Block Processing

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

In periods of competing blocks, Solana validators spend CPU and timing resources replaying blocks that will never make it into the canonical chain once another competing block from the same slot has been finalized.

This PR proposes changes to validator software to help prevent work from being done. It also decouples functionality and gives control to Votor in requesting slot cancellation without modifying BankForks.

Overall, this is a reasonable technical improvement and has a good engineering motivation. Further technical comments and review would be helpful to understand if there are potential race conditions or issues with reliability of replay and consensus. This could be split into two PRs to make it easier to test and review.

Make sure that the replay thread doesn't block on the scheduler finishing processing blocks.

Add slot cancellation, where Votor can tell replay which blocks to stop trying to process.

There was an earlier PR (PR #16454) which attempted to solve a similar problem, but that PR included some complexity around being able to pause and resume block processing.

This PR attempts to solve a similar problem in a simpler way by adding slot cancellation. It allows validators to stop replaying blocks that will never make it into the canonical chain once another block from the same slot has been finalized.

This is an efficiency-focused change to validator software. It's not intended to have a particular effect on transaction throughput or SOL price. For Solana to continue to perform well, it's important not only to continue to increase TPS but also continue to find ways to make sure that validators aren't doing unnecessary work.

For everyday users, it's unlikely there would be noticeable effects from this change. Sending/receiving SOL, using a DEX, using DeFi more broadly, and using any other Solana-powered website/app should all continue to function as normal. It's possible that users could see some benefits from this change in the form of Solana being more performant in the face of heavy compute loads.

#5073. Bitcoin Rebounds to $61K After Weekend Plunge to Two-Year Low

Bitcoin Rebounds to $61K After Weekend Plunge to Two-Year Low

Bitcoin recovered to around $61,300 early on Monday after a turbulent weekend that saw it fall as low as $55,298, its lowest level since September 2024, as a slide in tech stocks and expectations of tighter Federal Reserve policy rattled risk assets.

The leading cryptocurrency was up 0.5% over 24 hours at time of publication, but down 4.5% over the past week, according to CoinGecko data. It remains about 51% below its all-time high of $126,080.

The weekend low came a day after Bitcoin broke below $60,000 on Friday, as AI stocks slumped following Anthropic's IPO.

"Bitcoin's sharp volatility over the weekend was primarily the result of a steep pullback in U.S. tech stocks, expectations of further monetary policy tightening by the Federal Reserve, and deleveraging across global risk assets," Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey Group, told Decrypt.

If growth expectations keep falling while inflation keeps the Fed hiking, "two key pillars that previously supported risk-asset rallies—ample liquidity and strong growth expectations—could be weakened simultaneously," Sun said. More than $2 billion in leveraged liquidations over the weekend had released some short-term selling pressure, he added, creating conditions for a possible rebound.

Spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $669.2 million in net outflows on Friday, their largest single-day outflow since June 25, according to SoSoValue data. That brought last week's net outflows to $1.79 billion, the funds' third consecutive week of withdrawals topping $1 billion, and November's total so far to $4.14 billion, by Decrypt's calculation. Total net assets fell to $71.3 billion, the lowest since June 30.

"The weekend correction looks less like a Bitcoin-specific event and more like part of a wider market correction," Neil Steinhardt, head of Nexo U.S., told Decrypt, noting that gold and equities also fell. ETF outflows had worsened the drawdown, he said, adding that equities appeared to have led the sell-off.

It is now below its median since launch, while outflows run near $260M per day.

The last stretch this quiet, in mid-2024, came before the run to $100K. Periods of apathy tend to be better times to accumulate than periods of hype. pic.twitter.com/xiJ3HF9cLj

— glassnode (@glassnode) November 22, 2026

Onchain analytics firm Glassnode took a longer view. ETF trading volume has fallen below its median since the funds launched, while outflows are running near $260 million a day, the firm tweeted on Sunday. The last stretch this quiet, in mid-2024, preceded Bitcoin's run to $100,000, it said.

BitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes struck a more bearish note. Bitcoin had "decisively" broken below its previous local low, he tweeted on Saturday, adding that "$50,000 will be the next real test" if the Nasdaq kept falling. On Sunday evening, as Nasdaq futures weakened in Asian trading, Hayes tweeted that Bitcoin could retest $55,000, and noted that South Korea's Kospi index had fallen 5%.

$BTC just decisively broke below the previous local low. If Nasdaq keeps puking, $50,000 will be the next real test. pic.twitter.com/vn0VSpuWAz

— Arthur Hayes (@CryptoHayes) November 21, 2026

On Decrypt Predict, users put a 17% chance on Bitcoin falling to $55,000 before the end of November, as of 5:56 a.m. ET on Monday. The market settles on Binance's BTC/USDT price, which fell as low as $55,130 last week, according to the Binance chart Hayes shared. Users put a 1% chance on Bitcoin climbing back to $82,500 this month.

Traders now turn to October's personal consumption expenditures (PCE) inflation data, due on Wednesday, followed by the November jobs report on December 4 and the Fed's December 9 meeting.

The core PCE report "could help show whether the Fed is leaning toward 25 or 50 basis points," Steinhardt said, with markets then guided by the December meeting and comments from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh and other officials.

Traders are leaning toward the smaller move. As of 6:00 a.m. ET on Monday, CME FedWatch put the odds of a quarter-point hike on December 9 at 96.2%, up from 88.6% on Friday, with a 3.8% chance that rates stay unchanged. The odds of a half-point increase stood at zero, from 4.5% a week earlier.

U.S. spot selling remained heavy last week, according to a note from Bitfire Research shared with Decrypt. The Coinbase Bitcoin Premium Index, which tracks the gap between Bitcoin's price on Coinbase and on Binance, fell as low as negative 0.23%, the firm said.

Sun said he saw "no clear bullish catalyst" over the next one to two weeks, and expected Bitcoin to stay in a "high-volatility consolidation phase." Cooler inflation, steadier stocks and a return of ETF inflows could support a more sustainable recovery, he said, while hotter inflation and further tech losses could send Bitcoin back to its prior lows.

#5072. Microsoft’s ‘Code Red’ Exposes Crypto’s Own Cloud Problem

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Microsoft has reportedly declared a “Code Red” initiative to overhaul its engineering and crisis response following a global service outage that lasted approximately 24 hours. For an industry built around the idea of decentralization, crypto has good reason to pay attention.

According to internal memos reviewed by Reuters, the technology giant is reconsidering how it prevents and responds to major infrastructure failures after its November 12-13 outage disrupted businesses, government operations and financial firms.

Crypto likes to position itself as an alternative to centralized infrastructure. Yet some of its largest businesses depend on the same handful of cloud computing companies, and the consequences of that reliance have already been felt by traders.

In May, Coinbase experienced an infrastructure failure that demonstrated how surprisingly fragile access to cryptocurrency markets can be.

The exchange’s official incident report, published on June 1, traced the disruption to a cooling equipment failure inside an Amazon Web Services (AWS) data center.

Coinbase had five matching engine nodes located within the same building. Three went offline during the incident, leaving the system without enough functioning nodes to operate normally.

The exchange had not implemented an automated mechanism to switch its matching engine to another availability zone.

A separate failure involving AWS’s managed event-streaming infrastructure complicated the recovery further.

For approximately eight hours, customers experienced severe disruptions affecting trading, deposits and withdrawals. Restoring the remaining systems took roughly another 12 hours.

“The duration of the outage is unacceptable to us,” Coinbase acknowledged in its subsequent investigation.

This was not the first time the exchange had encountered such problems. An AWS outage in October 2025 resulted in three hours and 17 minutes of degraded performance for Coinbase customers.

Despite these incidents, the relationship between cryptocurrency businesses and cloud providers continues to deepen. More recently, Coinbase and AWS partnered to bring x402 payments to CloudFront publishers, bringing blockchain-based payments into existing web infrastructure.

The uncomfortable part is that the blockchains themselves did not need to fail for customers to lose access to exchange services.

A decentralized settlement network is of limited immediate use to someone whose assets are sitting inside an exchange they cannot access.

Moving assets away from centralized exchanges does reduce some of these risks. However, it does not necessarily eliminate reliance on centralized infrastructure.

When a user opens the application to check their balance or send a transaction, the wallet generally communicates with an Ethereum node through a remote procedure call, commonly known as an RPC.

That connection allows the application to retrieve blockchain information and submit signed transactions.

Many users rely on infrastructure operated by third-party providers rather than running their own nodes. If the provider becomes unavailable, the wallet may struggle to display balances or broadcast transactions, even while Ethereum continues producing blocks.

In an RPC service outage, the assets can remain intact on the blockchain even when the wallet’s usual connection to the network stops working.

Ethereum’s own node documentation acknowledges that widespread reliance on cloud hosting could introduce a common point of failure.

The distribution of Ethereum nodes also raises questions about infrastructure concentration. Having thousands of independently operated nodes does not necessarily eliminate shared dependencies if many rely on the same hosting providers.

Shared infrastructure can create security risks as well as availability problems. NewsBTC previously covered the debate over verifier and RPC security following the KelpDAO exploit. That incident was an exploit, not a routine cloud outage.

There are alternatives. Users can connect compatible wallets to another RPC provider or operate their own Ethereum nodes. Developers can also design applications to switch between independently operated infrastructure providers when one becomes unavailable.

But these options are not always obvious to the average person opening a wallet on their phone.

The industry has spent years making crypto easier to use, often by hiding much of its technical complexity. In doing so, it has sometimes reintroduced the dependencies that blockchain technology was intended to reduce.

It would be easy to criticize every cryptocurrency company that uses Amazon, Google or Microsoft infrastructure. The reality is more complicated.

Coinbase explained that keeping its matching engine nodes physically close together was a deliberate decision intended to meet the speed and capacity requirements of its markets.

Separating those systems introduces communication delays. Running redundant infrastructure also costs money, particularly when companies must synchronize large amounts of financial information across multiple locations.

Cloud computing providers offer considerable engineering resources and operational capabilities that smaller crypto companies would struggle to reproduce independently.

The problem is not simply that crypto businesses use centralized services. It is whether they have credible alternatives when those services fail.

Coinbase subsequently outlined plans to improve recovery across availability zones and conduct regular failover exercises in production environments.

Those are useful commitments, although publishing a recovery plan and successfully executing one during an unexpected outage are two different things.

There is no established evidence that Microsoft’s latest initiative was prompted by a failure of cryptocurrency networks. The relevance lies elsewhere.

As financial institutions bring more assets onto blockchains, the reliability of the infrastructure connecting investors to those networks becomes increasingly important.

A tokenized investment fund may exist on a distributed ledger, but investors can still depend on centralized custody providers, banking services, identity verification systems and applications to manage their holdings.

A decentralized exchange may execute trades through smart contracts, but its website and the infrastructure connecting users to those contracts can introduce separate vulnerabilities.

Crypto companies should be demonstrating how their products behave when their preferred infrastructure provider goes offline. Can users still submit transactions? Can traders cancel orders? Can another operator take over without waiting for an engineering team to intervene?

Microsoft’s reported response to its November outage is a reminder that even companies with enormous technical resources can discover weaknesses in systems they previously considered reliable.

Crypto does not need to abandon cloud computing. It needs to stop treating decentralization at the blockchain level as proof that everything built around it is equally resilient.

#5071. $600K stolen from Trezor and Exodus wallets – How did it happen?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Onchain Lens reported over $600,000 lost from one user’s Trezor and Exodus wallets on the 23rd of November. The Trezor wallet theft report raised a harder question: how did transfers use the victim’s signing authority without their claimed approval?

The blockchain investigator listed approximately $580,000 in Tether [USDT] losses on TRON and $23,400 in USD Coin [USDC] on Solana. Another $9,500 reportedly disappeared from an Exodus wallet on the same iPhone 17 Pro Max.

Reportedly, the victim generated the recovery phrase on Trezor and kept it on paper and refused to allow anyone physical access to the device.

A 49,999 USDT transfer on the 21st of November used the TRON account’s default owner permission. It was a direct transfer, with no transfer from operation drawing on an existing token allowance.

On Solana [SOL], the examined instruction identified the victim’s wallet as the transfer authority, signer, and fee payer. Notably, no separate delegate appeared.

These transfers used the wallet’s signing authority. However, it is unclear how someone gained that access.

A valid signature authorizes a transaction on the network. So, it cannot establish whether the owner knowingly approved it. The Trezor accounts on both chains shared one recovery phrase, making that backup a possible link between the losses.

In an X reply, Trezor said similar cases usually involved “a compromised wallet backup.”

It’s hard to say what happened here without more details.

The company asked the affected user to contact official support. Its reply offered a possible explanation, without establishing this incident’s cause.

Trezor says its Bluetooth chip cannot access private keys. On the other hand, Exodus says its Trezor integration also leaves those keys inside the hardware. Whether the user enabled that integration remains unclear.

Apple’s 9th of November update patched Bluetooth issues, but Onchain Lens found no evidence linking those vulnerabilities to these transfers.

Earlier incidents show why identifying the route matters.

As AMBCrypto reported, Trezor confirmed implants in three CryptoBilis-sold Safe 5 devices on the 12th of November. Those implants captured recovery words from device screens.

Separately, Confiant’s MoldyRoost research documented another route; malicious ads delivering exploits to vulnerable iPhones. Furthermore, Chainalysis counted roughly 158,000 personal-wallet compromise incidents affecting 80,000 victims in 2025.

For this user, the unanswered question is specific: how did someone obtain signing access across the affected wallets?

#5069. Solana Meme Coin for Fiona the Hippo Raises $100K for Cincinnati Zoo Charity

Solana Meme Coin for Fiona the Hippo Raises $100K for Cincinnati Zoo Charity

Fiona the Hippo, a fan-favorite pygmy hippo at the Cincinnati Zoo, died last week after swallowing a hat that accidentally ended up in her enclosure. Crypto bros have created a meme coin in her honor—raising $100,000 for charity in the process.

The tragic death came after a visitor tossed their knitted hat in the air, which then got caught by a ceiling fan and flung it through a small window into Fiona's habitat. The pygmy hippo lost her appetite as the hat got stuck in her small intestine, and veterinary staff tried their best to help Fiona pass the hat naturally—as surgery was deemed too risky. Unfortunately, Fiona died on Thursday, November 19, at nine years old.

As is often the case, crypto bros rushed to create a Solana meme coin that surged to a $3.52 million market capitalization the day after Fiona's death. It has since dropped more than 50% to $1.5 million, per DEX Screener.

Fiona the hippo has died after she ate a visitor's hat that fell into her enclosure at the Cincinnati Zoo. pic.twitter.com/YHbjoEEDhb

The Pump.fun-created token is donating 100% of the generated creator rewards to the Zoological Society of Cincinnati, the non-profit that runs the zoo and its scientific programs. So far, according to Donate.gg, $103,600 has been donated.

But, of course, profits are at the forefront of crypto traders' minds. One of the top traders turned a $1,637 investment into $43,800 in a matter of days, according to DEX Screener.

"I feel like animals are often treated more like attractions for people than living beings. Their safety and lives should come first, not just entertaining visitors," pseudonymous trader Athena Alpha told Decrypt. "This isn’t even the first time something like this has happened."

The most famous example happened in the same zoo. Endangered gorilla Harambe was fatally shot at the Cincinnati Zoo a decade ago, after a young boy fell into his habitat. This sparked global outrage, as the gorilla was killed through no fault of his own. In turn, Harambe became one of the most viral memes of the 2010s.

"I think stricter action needs to be taken against both visitors and zoo officials to make sure things like this don’t happen again," the trader said. "Honestly, I feel like a big part of the problem is the lack of accountability and consequences. Unless people are held responsible, nothing is really going to change."

The Cincinnati Zoo needs to ensure something like this can never happen again. https://t.co/vWeb8ekyVw pic.twitter.com/hqt35SOcP6

— Nati Sports (@Nati_Sports) November 19, 2026

This story has hit particularly hard, as Fiona was a beloved animal whose premature birth in 2017 drew attention. At birth, zoo keepers had to care for her because she was too small for her mother to look after. Fortunately, she survived this tough start to life and went on to become one of the zoo's most famous animals.

People's love for Fiona may have been boosted by the rise of Moo Deng, a cute pygmy hippo who went mega viral in 2024. As with Fiona, crypto traders made an unofficial meme coin for Moo Deng, but this one went much higher—peaking at a $610 million market cap.

Naturally, traders have made the comparison between the two pygmy hippos, with some suggesting that the Moo Deng meme coin's success should mean similar gains for the Fiona token.

With Fiona's meme coin sitting at a $1.5 million market cap, that thesis has yet to be proven.

"If Fiona goes to $1 billion, her legacy will live forever all around the world," one trader tweeted. "Do it for Fiona!"
