#5042. Best Crypto Wallets: Top 7 Picks for Max Security and Ease of Use

Home » Cryptopedia » Best Crypto Wallets: Top 7 Picks for Max Security and Ease of Use

Compare the top hardware and software crypto wallets to find your safest, easiest self-custody setup.

Keeping your cryptocurrency on an exchange is convenient, but it comes with risks. If the exchange gets hacked, freezes withdrawals, or runs into financial trouble, accessing your funds can become difficult. Using a self-custody wallet gives you direct control over your private keys and, ultimately, your crypto.

Whether you are holding Bitcoin for the next decade, trading memecoins on Solana, or exploring decentralized finance (DeFi), choosing the right wallet matters. Some wallets are designed to keep your assets as secure as possible, while others make it easier to trade, manage tokens, and connect to Web3 apps.

To help you find the right option, we’ve put together a list of seven popular crypto wallets, covering what each one does best, its main advantages, and what to consider before choosing it.

*Prices change frequently, so always confirm on the manufacturer’s official website.

If your primary goal is long-term wealth preservation, Ledger remains the industry benchmark for cold storage.

Unlike mobile apps that stay connected to the internet, Ledger devices store your private keys inside an offline, certified Secure Element chip, the same class of chip used in passports and credit cards (check Ledger’s website for the current certification details).

Through the Ledger Live companion app, you can buy, swap, and stake thousands of coins and tokens. Your private keys never leave the device. Ledger Live runs on your connected phone or computer, but transactions are signed on the Ledger itself.

For those who live by the motto “don’t trust, verify,” Trezor is the gold standard. Contrary to the competitors that keep parts of their code proprietary, Trezor’s firmware is fully open-source, meaning independent security researchers constantly audit it for vulnerabilities.

The Trezor Safe 5 pairs this transparency with a vibrant color touchscreen, haptic feedback, and an EAL6+ Secure Element. It also offers a dedicated Bitcoin-only firmware option for maximalists who want to minimize attack surfaces.

When it comes to interacting with decentralized applications (DApps), decentralized exchanges (DEXs), and NFT marketplaces, MetaMask is the undisputed gateway to Web3.

Available as both a browser extension and a mobile app, MetasMask connects seamlessly to virtually every Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) network, including Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon, Base, and BNB Chain.

Modern updates have expanded MetaMask beyond Ethereum via MetaMask Snaps and allow users to add support for non-EVM ecosystems like Bitcoin and Solana directly inside the same interface.

Originally built as the flagship wallet for the Solana ecosystem, Phantom has evolved into one of the fastest, cleanest multi-chain wallets on the market. Today, it seamlessly supports Solana, Ethereum, Base, Polygon, and Bitcoin in a single unified interface.

What sets Phantom apart is user experience. Transaction simulations show you exact balance changes before you hit approve, and its automated spam filter hides malicious airdrop NFTs so beginners don’t accidentally click phishing links.

If you want one smartphone app that holds virtually every cryptocurrency in existence without manual network configuration, Trust Wallet is built for you.

Supporting over 100 blockchains and millions of digital assets, it removes the technical friction of adding custom RPC networks or hunting down token contract addresses.

It also includes a built-in Web3 browser, straightforward in-app staking for major proof-of-stake coins, and an integrated Security Scanner that flags risky smart contracts.

Many newcomers confuse the main Coinbase exchange app with Coinbase Wallet, but they are completely separate products. Coinbase Wallet is a true non-custodial wallet—meaning you hold your own 12-word recovery phrase, and Coinbase cannot freeze or access your funds.

Note that the app’s branding has changed recently: Coinbase renamed it “Base App” in July 2025 and restored the Coinbase Wallet name in September 2026. It has since shifted toward multichain trading, including perpetual futures, prediction markets, and tokenized stocks, so some of its features are now aimed at more active traders.

Its biggest advantage is frictionless onboarding. You can link your exchange account to transfer funds into self-custody in seconds, claim a free human-readable username instead of copying long hexadecimal addresses, and explore Base and Ethereum DApps.

Traditional hardware wallets require cables, batteries, and carefully guarding a 24-word paper backup. Tangem reimagines cold storage as a sleek, waterproof smart card—roughly the size and thickness of a standard bank debit card.

To approve a transaction, you simply tap the card against the back of your NFC-enabled smartphone. Tangem comes in sets of two or three cards that act as physical backups for one another, allowing you to skip vulnerable paper seed phrases entirely (though a traditional seed option is still available if you prefer it).

Understanding the difference between hot and cold storage saves you from overpaying—or worse, leaving your funds exposed:

A common rule of thumb among experienced crypto investors is to use both, for example keeping around 90% of long-term holdings in a cold wallet and about 10% in a hot wallet for everyday trading and Web3 exploration. This is a guideline, not a standard – adjust it to your own situation.

With crypto, there’s no bank to call if something goes wrong. Transactions are usually irreversible, and if an exchange freezes withdrawals or goes bankrupt, your funds could be stuck for months or even years.

That’s why choosing the best crypto wallet matters. It gives you more control over your money and lets you manage your funds without relying on an exchange.

Your cryptocurrency is not stored inside the physical device—it lives on the blockchain. If your Ledger, Trezor, or Tangem card is lost, stolen, or broken, you can buy a replacement device and restore full access to your funds in minutes using your 12- or 24-word recovery phrase (or backup Tangem card).

While no system is 100% immune, cold hardware wallets cannot be hacked remotely because your private keys stay offline. Most wallet “hacks” happen when users accidentally sign a malicious smart contract on a phishing website or store their seed phrase digitally where malware can find it.

Software wallets like MetaMask, Phantom, and Trust Wallet are completely free to download and hold crypto in. Hardware wallets require an upfront purchase (typically $55 to $250). Regardless of the wallet you choose, you will still pay standard blockchain network (“gas”) fees whenever you send or swap tokens.

With a custodial wallet (like a standard exchange account), a third-party company holds your private keys and can freeze or restrict your withdrawals. With a non-custodial (self-custody) wallet, only you hold the private keys—meaning nobody can block your transactions, though you are solely responsible for backing up your recovery phrase.

No. Unlike traditional bank accounts, funds in a self-custody crypto wallet are not covered by government deposit insurance like the FDIC or SIPC. Because you act as your own bank, protecting your recovery phrase and verifying transaction details before approving them is your primary safeguard.

#5041. LINK, AAVE and UNI Now Supported by Fidelity

Fidelity Investments now supports three new cryptocurrencies on its retail crypto trading platform: Chainlink (LINK), Aave (AAVE) and Uniswap (UNI).

The firm expanded from five available cryptocurrencies to eight on Nov. 24. In just one day, Fidelity added the same number of digital assets that it had added in the four years since it first made Bitcoin and Ether available for customer trading.

Eligible U.S. customers can trade these three tokens on the Fidelity website and app. Some states may have limited access to Fidelity's services.

Fidelity's three new listings include tokens that represent different areas of decentralized finance. Aave is a lending protocol where users can deposit crypto assets to earn interest or use them as collateral for loans. AAVE token holders can vote on changes to the protocol's lending markets and other aspects of its operation.

Uniswap is a decentralized trading platform where users can trade different tokens using shared pools of assets provided by other users. UNI is the Uniswap governance token.

Chainlink provides the data that blockchain apps need to operate. For example, a lending protocol might use a Chainlink price feed to assess the value of collateral for a borrower's loan. Chainlink (LINK) tokens are used to pay for services provided on its network.

Fidelity Crypto started accepting customers from its waitlist in November 2022. At the time, the only two cryptocurrencies it offered were Bitcoin (BTC) and Ether (ETH). By March 2023, Fidelity was offering its service to more eligible U.S. investors, but these were still the only cryptocurrencies it allowed customers to trade.

On July 17, 2024, Fidelity added Litecoin (LTC) to its list of cryptocurrencies, bringing the total to three. Over a year later, on Oct. 23, 2025, the company introduced Solana (SOL). In addition to individual retail accounts, Solana became available for crypto IRAs, wealth managers and institutional clients.

Fidelity added its fifth cryptocurrency on Feb. 4, 2026, when it launched Fidelity Digital Dollar (FIDD) as its first stablecoin available to retail and institutional investors. Eligible users can exchange or redeem each FIDD token for $1. Fidelity waives its usual crypto trading fee when users exchange FIDD for dollars.

#5040. Prediction market bets placed just before big news could soon be easier to trace

New CFTC reporting rules could help investigators trace prediction market trades to people with early access to information.

The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) approved a rule on Nov. 23 requiring exchanges that list certain prediction market contracts to collect traders' names and employers.

When trading surges ahead of an announcement, those records could help investigators identify who traded and look for links to people or organizations with early access to the news.

The final rule also requires exchanges to disclose when covered trades occurred, at what price and size, and how the contracts settled. The CFTC says the reports will help it monitor trading across markets.

Under Section 16.03, exchanges must publish each covered trade’s execution time, ticker, size, and US dollar price as soon as technologically practicable.

The data must stay free for at least a year after it first appears, with instructions on how to download, save, and search it. Public trade disclosure is familiar to exchanges such as Kalshi.

A May 13 CFTC staff letter already made prompt publication of those four fields and reporting to the CFTC under Section 16.02 conditions of relief from certain swap-reporting rules. Its updated list includes KalshiEX and Kalshi Klear.

On Nov. 23, Kalshi’s public trade feed recorded a match for 981.95 contracts in KXHIGHNY-26NOV23-T64 at one cent for Yes and 99 cents for No. The $1 binary contract asked whether New York City’s high that day would fall below 64°F.

Kalshi’s product filing identifies the exchange as a registered designated contract market. Its clearing affiliate, Kalshi Klear, told the CFTC that it clears KalshiEX’s binary event-contract swaps on a fully cash-collateralized basis.

The reporting rule covers certain event contracts classified as swaps and listed on a designated contract market.

A derivatives clearing organization must clear the contract and hold enough collateral at all times to cover the maximum possible loss. A covered contract can pay a fixed amount to one side, or pay both sides based on the settlement price in a structure where only one side profits.

The contract named The Weather Company as the source for its outcome. Kalshi’s settlement record shows a high of 69°F and a final No, with settlement recorded at 12:07 p.m. UTC on Nov. 24. The rule requires exchanges to publish whether the event occurred and, if it did, what happened, when it happened, and the source used to determine the outcome.

A reader could line up the execution timestamps with an independently verified announcement time and see which trades came first. Kalshi’s trade ID identifies the execution, and the public feed shows the trades in sequence, while the accounts behind them remain private.

Exchanges will have to collect each trader’s name, physical address, email, phone number, occupation, and employer and associate that information with every covered order or trade.

The rule also calls for the names of account guarantors and people with a financial interest of 10% or more in the trader or account, where applicable. Exchanges must keep the data for the life of the contract and for at least five years after it ends.

The CFTC’s reporting guidebook shows how the agency can use a customer account number to match an exchange’s trade report with a separate file that lists the trader’s occupation and employer.

A link to a company involved in an announcement could help investigators decide where to look. They would still need to establish when the information became available, whether the trader had access to it, and whether their conduct violated the relevant rule.

A covered execution has a public trade entry and a separate CFTC report. Account numbers, with other identifiers when needed, connect the regulatory report to a customer file.

Public trade reporting starts 60 days after Federal Register publication. Exchanges have 12 months from publication to meet the new identity collection requirement.

Under Section 16.02, exchanges report identifying data they already maintain once the provision applies to covered trades. An employer match can guide an inquiry. A finding of misconduct requires separate evidence of conduct.

The public branch shows the fields in Section 16.03(f). The regulatory branch follows the CFTC guidebook’s account-number match between the Trade Capture Report and Customer Account Reference file.

Under Section 16.02, exchanges report identifying data they already maintain once the provision applies to covered trades. An employer match can guide an inquiry. A finding of misconduct requires separate evidence of conduct.

A Nov. 24 Federal Register search for the rule’s identification number still showed only the July proposal. The rule takes effect 60 days after the final text appears in the Register.

The public trade and settlement disclosures and the duty to report under Section 16.02 start at the same time.

Exchanges have 12 months from Federal Register publication to comply with the new identity-collection requirement for prediction market contracts.

Once Section 16.02 applies, the CFTC expects exchanges to report identifying data they already maintain. The separate large-trader provisions start 60 days after publication or on July 26, 2027, whichever is later.

#5039. Tether’s USDT loses $8.83B in 60 days – Is a 2022-style crash coming?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

USDT’s market cap may now be a key metric to watch for signs of a market bottom.

Technically, Tether’s USDT is experiencing its most severe quarterly de-pegging since Q2 2022, which saw over 18% of its market cap drained away, totalling roughly $15 billion. Although currently the de-pegging figure is lower (around -5% so far in Q4), the consequence remains impactful. Since 2022, USDT’s market cap has increased to almost $180 billion from approximately $80 billion. This means even a smaller percentage drop now represents a much larger amount of liquidity leaving the market.

The chart below highlights this trend. According to CryptoQuant data, USDT’s market cap has fallen by $8.83 billion over the 60 days leading up to the 22nd of November. Furthermore, its 30-day Moving Average is also falling, which indicates the decline is still in motion.

To put this into perspective, back in 2022 a 5% fall in Tether’s [USDT] $80 billion market cap would have caused approximately $4 billion worth of liquidity to exit the market. However, when applying the same 5% market cap reduction to today’s $180 billion figure, almost $9 billion is now leaving the market. That’s more than 2x the amount of liquidity being pulled out for the same percentage decline.

In this context, USDT’s growing market cap means its contraction now has a much bigger impact on liquidity.

Tether’s ongoing contraction further adds to the liquidity concerns.

TVL on DeFi platforms has decreased to just over $70 billion. This is from an approximate figure of $140 billion prior to the October 2025 crash. Thus, in just over a year, the TVL on DeFi platforms has almost been cut in half. Coupled with the reduction in USDT’s market cap, this suggests there is poor liquidity and reduced capital involvement within the crypto space.

However, the impact goes beyond DeFi liquidity. As the chart below shows, the broader crypto market has also experienced a significant bear run. So far in Q4, the market has lost over 28% of its value, reducing the market cap from $2.84 trillion down to below $1.8 trillion, meaning almost $500 billion has been erased. The key takeaway? This is the worst quarterly fall for the crypto market since Q2 2022, which also witnessed the largest-ever de-pegging of Tether’s USDT stablecoin.

According to AMBCrypto, this overlap is not random.

Rather, with Tether’s market cap now much larger than it was in 2022, even a small drop in USDT supply is now having a bigger impact on overall market liquidity. This makes USDT supply an important metric to watch during the current downturn.

Until USDT’s market cap bottoms, a sustained crypto market bottom may remain out of reach.

DeFi TVL has nearly halved to $70 billion, while the broader crypto market is down over 28% in Q4.

USDT’s shrinking market cap points to continued liquidity outflows, making its recovery a key signal to watch for a market bottom.

#5038. Bitcoin Rallies, Anthropic Sinks as Nvidia Surges 35% on Jensen Huang’s Return

Bitcoin Rallies, Anthropic Sinks as Nvidia Surges 35% on Jensen Huang’s Return

Wall Street welcomed Jensen Huang back to Nvidia with lots of green confetti today by sending the chipmaker’s shares up nearly 35%, helping drag battered technology stocks and crypto prices out of last week’s rout.

Nvidia traded around $169.83 at 10:28 a.m. ET, up 34.97% from Friday’s close. It is the biggest bullish jump in the history of the company.

And the FOMO contagion spread quickly to other tech stocks. Rival AMD jumped 8.91% to $462.09, while the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) surged 15% to $141.77.

You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Nvidia with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.

Bitcoin joined the party, trading near $63,500 after dipping below $60,000 during Friday’s selloff. Ethereum climbed to about $1,790, and cash CFDs tracking the Nasdaq 100 and S&P 500 rebounded to roughly 26,950 and 7,285, respectively.

The catalyst was Nvidia’s announcement that its founder Jensen Huang had been reinstated as president, CEO and director, effective immediately. The board voted unanimously just six days after publicly ruling out his return—and even doubling down on their decision several times.

Huang resigned November 12 amid reports of extramarital relationships, including one with a businesswoman U.S. officials suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence. Beijing has denied the espionage allegation, and no public evidence has established that Huang knowingly passed company secrets to China.

Colette Kress, Nvidia’s finance chief, took over as interim CEO while the company launched a search for a permanent replacement. On November 17, board chair Harvey Jones said directors did not intend to reinstate Huang, despite a campaign for his return backed by Silicon Valley executives and President Donald Trump.

Monday’s reversal followed meetings with Huang and input from senior U.S. government officials. The board said it was satisfied with his candor and leadership ability and was confident his return posed “no national security risk,” though its independent investigation will continue.

“I can’t wait to get back to work,” Huang said in the statement. Kress will remain chief financial officer, and Jones will stay on as board chair.

“It tells us to some extent that Jensen Huang was too big to be fired,” Interactive Brokers strategist Steve Sosnick told Reuters.

Prediction markets were caught off guard, too. A Polymarket contract on Huang rejoining Nvidia by November 30 traded near 99% after the announcement, compared with roughly 3% shortly beforehand.

His return also tanked the probabilities of the AI bubble bursting. After his outsting, Polymarket odds skyrocketed to more than 70%, minutes after his reinstatement, the odds dropped to 14%.

The rally followed an ugly stretch for AI stocks. Nvidia closed Friday at $125.53, about 47.5% below its October high, while the Nasdaq lost roughly 10% over the previous week. Bitcoin fell toward $55,100 Friday night before staging a weekend recovery.

Monday’s bounce pushed Nvidia above the $166.19 closing price recorded on the day Huang resigned. Bitcoin, meanwhile, recovered the $63,000 area, but its daily chart still shows a bearish moving-average configuration and a relative strength index near 34, indicating that the recent relief rally has not erased the broader downtrend.

Overall, crypto traders are still timid but evidently don’t think this is the end of the world.

On the chart, Bitcoin faces initial resistance around $65,030, followed by $68,090. On the downside, $61,240 and the psychological $60,000 mark are immediate levels to watch; another break lower would put the recent $55,100 area back in focus.

One of the few notable losers was Anthropic, whose stock slipped 3.16% to $85.81. That left the Claude developer about 25% below its post-IPO peak near $115, although still slightly above the $83 offering price set for its $81.34 billion public offering last Thursday. Nvidia itself committed about $10 billion to a separate, conditional private investment in Anthropic alongside the IPO.

The decline looks more like investors continuing to digest a pricey, volatile listing than a reaction to Huang’s reinstatement. But the internet has another theory: memes and posts have cast Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei as playing a role in Huang’s ouster because of his support towards open-weight models and his decision to buy Hugging Face, the world’s largest repository of open source AI models, to protect the ecosystem.

Huang championed broad access to open models, while Amodei has argued for tighter safeguards around powerful AI systems, especially warning against open source AI competing against close models like the ones his company develops, a position that has been widely criticized by influential figures in the AI scene like Yan Lecun who called his mindset “a new form of medieval obscurantism.”

Dario's spiel since GPT-2 has always been about hyping the dangers so that open models would be made illegal and *he* would stay in control.He left OpenAI because he wasn't going to have control.It's like the Ottoman Empire banning the printing press for Arabic so they would…

Nvidia’s independent inquiry into the reported foreign intelligence effort remains open. Huang has also been asked to meet House investigators on December 1 and testify before a Senate panel on December 3.

#5037. Ansem claims wallet hack after an 87 million ANSEM token dump, but on-chain data raises questions

Ansem claims his Solana wallet was hacked after 87.49 million ANSEM tokens were sold, sending the memecoin tumbling 57%.

Crypto trader Ansem said his Pump wallet was hacked on Tuesday, roughly 51 minutes after a Solana wallet labeled “ansemconzimp” on Pump.fun finished selling about 87.49 million ANSEM, according to a Coindaro tally.

In his post, Ansem said he suspected someone had accessed his Bullpen profile, a trading app where he said he had imported the wallet’s Solana private key. In a later reply, Ansem denied making the trades and said he was conducting a security audit.

Ansem also said he believed the activity was limited to Solana. He said Bullpen was the only place he had imported his private key and that he didn't think anyone had accessed his Ethereum-compatible Pump wallets.

Solscan’s wallet page lists the Pump.fun name “ansemconzimp” and identifies the wallet as the owner of the token account for The Black Bull, the token that trades as ANSEM.

Coindaro counted 25 ANSEM sales from 08:57 to 10:08 UTC on Nov. 24, with about 21,520 SOL received. It reported that the wallet began the period with about 87.48 million ANSEM and received a few thousand more while selling was underway, accounting for the slightly higher total sold.

Solscan showed about 85 ANSEM in the token account later that afternoon.

A transaction tally and a public statement track two moments in the Nov. 24 sell-off.

The public records leave who authorized the sales unresolved.

Ansem gave no wallet address in his post. Solscan’s label reflects a public Pump.fun profile.

Times come from Coindaro’s ANSEM tally and Ansem’s post and are shown to the nearest minute in UTC. Positions are proportional to those times. The gap is 10:59 minus 10:08. Arbiscan’s snapshot is rounded to two decimals in millions of USDC.

Ansem gave no wallet address in his post. Solscan’s label reflects a public Pump.fun profile.

In July, Ansem said he held 58% of ANSEM’s supply. Coindaro’s Nov. 24 tally covers sales from one address.

Bitquery also tracked a wider burst of Solana memecoin sales by the wallet that morning, measuring a 57% price drop in under an hour, from $0.0367 to $0.0158.

An Arbitrum address highlighted by blockchain tracker Lookonchain held about 2.57 million USDC at 15:34 UTC, and Bitquery traced transfers through the Relay bridge, finding that some of the stablecoin reached the address before the first ANSEM sale.

Lookonchain also flagged the sales at 09:39 UTC and asked whether the wallet had been hacked. At 09:55 UTC, it said the activity looked like a hack and pointed to an address on Arbitrum as the destination for funds.

In an afternoon update, it characterized about $2.57 million as stolen.

On-chain researcher MLM questioned the hack account, saying that an older wallet he had labeled as Ansem’s sent funds to the eventual recipient before the selling began. Bitquery also traced early payments from an older Solana address and said it could not identify its owner.

#5036. US Moves to Recover $1.1 Billion From Binance Hack, Saylor's Strategy Buys 457 BTC, XRP Briefly Reclaims $1 — U.Today Crypto Digest

Monday brought a sharp rebound across crypto markets after Bitcoin's weekend crash toward $55,000.

XRP briefly reclaimed $1 as a short squeeze followed a major Nvidia-related rally, while Strategy continued adding Bitcoin to its treasury despite the market downturn.

Meanwhile, U.S. authorities took action to recover more than $1.1 billion in cryptocurrency linked to the October Binance hack.

The U.S. Department of Justice filed a civil forfeiture action on Nov. 23 seeking to recover more than $1.1 billion in USDC allegedly stolen from Binance by North Korean hackers.

The assets had previously been frozen under a restraining order obtained by the government. The latest filing represents another step toward recovering funds following the Oct. 29 attack, which reportedly resulted in more than $6 billion in stolen cryptocurrency.

The DOJ claimed that its recent civil forfeiture action focuses on over $1.1 billion worth of USD Coin (USDC), a stablecoin pegged 1:1 to the U.S. dollar and issued by Circle.

U.S. authorities said they had helped freeze, seize or return more than $2.9 billion in cryptocurrency since the theft. The case highlights the role of cooperation between law enforcement agencies and crypto companies in tracking and recovering stolen digital assets.

Strategy purchased another 457 BTC for approximately $29.6 million, according to a Nov. 23 report based on the company's SEC filing.

The latest acquisition was made at an average price of $64,898 per Bitcoin, bringing Strategy's holdings to approximately 851,305 BTC. The company has spent around $64.23 billion accumulating Bitcoin at an average purchase price of $75,446.

The firm's recent purchase comes as the leading cryptocurrency has been struggling to rebound from the heavy sell-off that recently dragged it to a two-plus-year low.

XRP briefly climbed above $1 on Monday after Nvidia's Jensen Huang returned to his roles as CEO and president, triggering a sharp rally in U.S. technology stocks and broader risk assets.

On Binance's XRP/USDT perpetual contract, the token moved from approximately $0.94 to $1.02 within minutes after 14:00 UTC, before retreating to around $0.984.

CoinGlass data cited by U.Today showed that XRP short liquidations exceeded long liquidations by 578%.

Across the crypto market, 110,663 traders were liquidated for $660.89 million over the past 24 hours, while shorts accounted for $515.94 million of that amount.

The move showed how quickly market sentiment can shift during a volatile rebound, particularly when leveraged traders are positioned against a sudden price increase.

For SharpLink, the move is also linked to its Ethereum treasury strategy. The company aims to increase its ETH per share, which measures how much Ethereum backs each outstanding company share.

Here, it’s worth noting that Ethereum’s Taker Buy/Sell Ratio has remained largely below 1 throughout November 2026, indicating that aggressive selling volume exceeded aggressive buying volume across exchanges. At press time, the ratio stood at 0.98, hinting at sustained selling pressure and relatively weak buying demand.

Additionally, CoinShares recently sold its entire Ethereum holdings in October, generating $19.3 million. Given that it will use these millions to repurchase its own shares under a $40 million buyback program, caution makes sense.

#5034. End of Crypto Trading? How AI Replaces Ones Who Pumped Bitcoin (BTC)

The “pump” trade could be taken to new extremes. While some may still be able to use their influence to promote a token, causing others to pile in, it could now be left up to AI to scour socials/wallet activity for abnormal trading volume, assess momentum rankings, etc. and execute on these opportunities faster than those that may be slower to react.

All things considered, agents may exacerbate many of the existing issues with crypto, from short lived moves/reversals, to dangerous herding and even more pronounced drawdowns.

Automation is not necessarily a new occurrence in the space, from simple rule-based trading (implement a certain set of rules when X occurs) to algo trading (use algos to spread out trading activity to avoid market impact), but it appears to be shifting from humans implementing strategies to letting AI make decisions and execute.

A February 2026 study from the Journal of Futures Markets found sub-second trading patterns in BTC/ETH perpetual/spot markets exhibiting behavior consistent with algo trading for liquidity, increasing volatility and trading costs with no significant impact on prices.

In August 2026, Binance rolled out Agent OS allowing builders to access exchange trading functionality and data via AI agents.

Coinbase Ventures released a comprehensive breakdown of the crypto agentic stack from data, to agent building tools, to execution/compliance in November. Instead of dictating each trade, users may be able to assign high-level goals (i.e. follow momentum, hedge position, etc.) for agents to implement 24/7.

Automation will likely accelerate across the crypto space. While macro events, ETF inflows/outflows, large holders, etc. will still have an impact on Bitcoin, it’s likely that many more aspects/trades will become automated.

Time will tell how pervasive agentic trading will become, but the era of a small group of traders/influencers/chat rooms able to move the needle via FOMO/hype seems poised to face stiff competition from AI that never sleeps.

AI is not necessarily intelligent. A 2026 study published in the journal Frontiers in Blockchain studied machine-learning strategies using crypto market data and found that many strategies became highly overfit and offered no viable edge for retail traders once realistic trading fees were taken into account.

Also, strategies that performed well on one cryptocurrency did not necessarily perform well on others. Faster processing speeds can’t make bad data good, can’t identify all false narratives and can’t insulate a strategy from sudden shifts in market regimes.

Are institutional investors still relevant? Can they protect themselves? Absolutely.

Institutions are (and will continue to be) an important source of capital, liquidity and price discovery (particularly for Bitcoin). A 2026 study using BTC data from 2012–2025 found that as the market has matured, Bitcoin has seen increased trading volume, decreasing transaction costs and increasing market efficiency.

Wintermute reported that in the first half of 2026 institutional clients accounted for 72% of total spot trading volume on its OTC desk (note: this is Wintermute’s OTC desk and is not representative of the entire market). It’s also worth noting that many institutional investors do employ quantitative strategies and state-of-the-art execution technologies.

While larger investors may have access to better data, faster infrastructure, cross-venue surveillance capabilities and stricter risk management protocols (and can limit their exposure and monitor abnormal order flow), there’s only so much that institutional investors can do to protect themselves.

Institutional investors can’t control a 24/7 global market with liquidity spread across multiple venues and derivatives markets. They also can’t assume that all AIs are created equal/safe (as Binance’s launch of its own AI demonstrated prompt injection risks and limited visibility into external AIs’ trading logic/reasons for trading).

Finally, during times of stress, risk management/contingency protocols (used by many investors) could be a crowded exit for funds that employ similar strategies.

The future is not “AI replaces every trader.” It will likely see continued automation of certain aspects of trading (i.e. execution, short-term alpha hunting, etc.) and a continued shift in the value-add that humans bring to the table (i.e. capital allocation, risk management, original research, granting/trading bots permission to trade, etc.).

While AI/bots may continue to squeeze spreads in normal market conditions, they may exacerbate drawdowns/cascades during times of market stress as strategies compete with one another.

At the end of the day, Bitcoin will still be bought/sold, it’s just a question of who gets to make those decisions.

#5033. Tom Lee Says Ethereum Is as Scarce as Bitcoin—And Bitmine Just Bought More

Tom Lee Says Ethereum Is as Scarce as Bitcoin—And Bitmine Just Bought More

Bitmine Immersion Technologies kept its weekly Ethereum buying streak alive, adding 7,819 ETH worth roughly $13.8 million, as chairman Tom Lee leaned on a new argument for the battered token: its supply grows no faster than Bitcoin’s, making it just as much “hard money.”

The NYSE-listed company said Monday its holdings reached 6,085,564 ETH, worth roughly $10.4 billion at a reference price of $1,713 per coin, as of Nov. 22.

That’s 4.98% of Ethereum’s 122.2 million token supply, leaving Bitmine 99% of the way to its goal of owning 5% of the network, the “Alchemy of 5%” target it has chased for 17 months. The firm has bought Ethereum every week since launching its treasury strategy on June 30, 2025.

You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Ethereum with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.

Lee’s pitch this week centered on scarcity. Since Bitmine pivoted to Ethereum in mid-2025, he said, ETH’s supply has grown just 0.90% on an annualized basis, roughly in line with Bitcoin’s 0.82%, meaning “both are ‘hard money’ measured in supply growth.” (Disclosure: Tom Lee is one of several investors in Dastan, Decrypt’s parent company.)

He contrasted that with more inflationary rivals, citing annualized supply growth of 7.6% for Solana, 5.4% for XRP, and 2.9% for Cardano. The framing builds on Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin’s recent declaration that ETH is a store of value, which Lee has repeatedly invoked.

Counting cash, other tokens and “moonshot” investments, Bitmine’s total holdings stood at $11.1 billion, including 216 Bitcoin, $384 million in cash and marketable securities, a $180 million stake in Beast Industries and a $54 million position in Eightco Holdings.

Bitmine remains the world’s largest Ethereum treasury and the second-largest crypto treasury overall, behind Michael Saylor’s Strategy, which the release said holds 849,327 BTC.

Strategy also kept buying through the downturn, recently adding $30 million in Bitcoin while shifting $1 billion from its dollar reserve to a cash pot.

The purchase lands as crypto claws back some ground after a bruising November. Bitcoin traded around $62,700 on Monday, up about 3.2% on the day, with Ethereum near $1,769, up 3.5%, as risk appetite steadied.

The rebound coincided with a dramatic reversal at Nvidia, which reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO just days after its board had ruled out his return, lifting sentiment across the AI-linked assets that crypto increasingly tracks.

Bitmine has 5,227,037 ETH, about 86% of its holdings, staked through its MAVAN platform, with projected annualized staking revenue of roughly $245 million.

#5031. Bitcoin’s $60,000 bear market is testing miners harder than the 2022 crypto winter

Bitcoin’s hashrate rebounds as mining revenue per unit hits $29.36 and AI competes for power and infrastructure.

Bitcoin’s hashrate rebounded above 1,000 exahashes per second in the week to Nov. 23, while the expected dollar revenue per unit of that computing power fell over the same week.

Luxor’s weekly mining update put the seven-day average hashrate at 1,033 EH/s, up 7.8% from 959 EH/s a week earlier.

Over the same week, dollar hashprice fell 3%, from $30.27 to $29.36 per petahash per second per day. Hashprice is the gross daily revenue a miner can expect from a fixed amount of computing power, before electricity and other costs.

The rebound came with Bitcoin trading near $60,000 on Nov. 24, about 52.5% below its October 2025 price record. The 30-day average hashrate was about 1,013 EH/s on Nov. 23, or 91.2% of the roughly 1,110 EH/s high recorded on Nov. 11, 2025, in the period analyzed.

The average had fallen to 896 EH/s on July 28, about 19.3% below that high.

The same point in the two previous Bitcoin bear markets gives that 91% some context.

The comparison uses the 30-day average 413 days after each cycle’s peak daily price close, measured against the highest 30-day hashrate recorded between the price peak and day 413.

It also uses Blockchain.com’s daily estimates, with Coin Metrics readings filling three missing dates in November 2025. A 30-day average smooths swings when blocks arrive more quickly or slowly by chance.

In the 2017–18 cycle, mining power kept rising after the December 2017 price peak. It reached 52.4 EH/s in October 2018, then fell to 37.6 EH/s on Dec. 25. By Feb. 2, 2019, the matched date, it had recovered to 41.9 EH/s, just under 80% of its high.

In the 2021–22 cycle, hashrate also set a high well after the price peak, reaching 265.2 EH/s in November 2022. It stood at 246.8 EH/s on Dec. 26, 2022, or 93.1% of its high. Today’s network is slightly farther below its peak than it was at that point in 2022 and closer than it was after the 2018 slump.

Bitcoin’s 30-day network hashrate as a share of its cycle high, measured 413 days after each peak daily price close. Each high is the strongest 30-day estimate from the price peak through the comparison date.

Source: Blockchain.com 2017–19 · · Blockchain.com 2020–22 · · Blockchain.com 2024–26 · · Coin Metrics, November 2025 · · Galaxy Research, price peaks · · Blockchain.com, methodology

Hashrate Index recorded a 2022 hashprice low of $55.94 per petahash per second per day, almost twice its Nov. 23 reading. The April 2024 halving cut Bitcoin’s fixed subsidy from 6.25 to 3.125 BTC per block. Transaction fees add to that subsidy, but they made up just 0.64% of block rewards in Luxor’s latest weekly snapshot.

Bitcoin’s mining difficulty fell 9.13% on Nov. 14. Using power prices and machine economics, Luxor’s West Texas analysis estimated that miners cutting electricity use there could account for roughly three-quarters of the 91 EH/s drop in the network’s 14-day average around that adjustment.

Riot Platforms previously earned credits for reducing power use.

Core Scientific’s third-quarter results show $215.4 million in quarterly colocation revenue, and the company was billing for 485 megawatts of capacity as of Sept. 30.

IREN said its Horizon 1 facility entered service for Microsoft during the September quarter. The company’s mining revenue fell to $28 million from $67 million in the previous quarter.

Riot’s November results show the company mined 1,637 BTC in the third quarter, up from 1,406 a year earlier, and separately disclosed a 910-megawatt powered-land lease for AI at Corsicana with the first delivery scheduled for September 2027.

A sustained loss of mining power would lengthen the expected time between blocks at the prevailing difficulty.

Bitcoin adjusts the difficulty every 2,016 blocks to bring the pace back toward one block every 10 minutes.

#5030. Bitwise XRP ETF Averages $14 Million in Daily Trading in Year One

The Bitwise XRP ETF traded an average of about $14 million a day over its first year on the market, resulting in over $3.5 billion in total trading volume, according to Bitwise.

In a post on X commemorating the Bitwise XRP ETF's first anniversary, Bitwise said the fund had recorded over $667 million in net inflows and had more than $376 million in assets under management (AUM) since launch.

Bitwise's XRP ETF started trading on Nov. 20, 2025, on NYSE Arca. It trades under the same ticker as the cryptocurrency it holds, XRP.

Investors can use the ETF's shares to track the price of the token through their brokerage accounts. The fund holds the XRP on behalf of investors. At launch, the ETF charged a 0.34% annual management fee. It also offered a fee waiver for the first $500 million in assets for the first month.

The $3.5 billion in trading volume is the total value of purchases and sales of the ETF's shares. This means the same ETF shares could trade repeatedly. If an investor sells their shares to another investor, that transaction increases trading volume. But the total XRP held in the fund doesn't change in that case.

On the other hand, the $667 million in net inflows represents the total dollar value of new shares issued over the past year minus redeemed shares.

AUM represents the total dollar value of a fund's assets at a specific moment. Since the fund's total assets are valued in dollars, AUM can fall below cumulative net inflows if the price of XRP declines, even as investors continue to put money into the fund.

The quarterly report filed by Bitwise with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) shows the impact of investor demand and XRP's price on the fund over the past year.

The net asset value of the fund increased from $299.1 million at the end of June to $614.9 million at the end of September.

Over $315.7 million was added to the fund's net assets during that quarter. Just over half of that $315.7 million came from new share creations.

The fund issued new shares with a total dollar value of $210.7 million. It also redeemed $32.8 million in shares during that quarter. So that left about $178 million in net new creations.

The fund issued 13.75 million shares and redeemed 2.42 million shares.

#5029. Bitcoin faces a familiar macro threat as the US prepares another round of tariffs

A reported US tariff push targeting 16 economies could reignite trade tensions and expose Bitcoin to renewed market volatility.

The Wall Street Journal reported on Nov. 24 that the US was preparing higher tariffs on China, the European Union, and other trading partners, which could impact Bitcoin.

Citing people familiar with the plans, the Journal reported that US Trade Representative (USTR) Jamieson Greer could release the findings of a months-long investigation into manufacturing overcapacity as soon as this week.

On Nov. 24, the USTR docket still showed the investigation opened in March and four days of hearings in May, listing no determination or tariff schedule for the case. A check of published USTR notices in the Federal Register found none dated Nov. 19 through Nov. 24.

The available White House, Treasury, and Commerce trade agency listings carried no announcement of the action described in the report. Importers still have no published list of the goods that would face these duties, the rates that would apply or the date they would start.

On Nov. 20, Greer told Bloomberg Television he expected the work to be finished by year-end. He declined to specify which economies might face additional tariffs.

USTR opened the investigations on March 11 under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 and is examining whether policies such as subsidies sustain more manufacturing capacity than demand supports and whether those practices burden or restrict US commerce.

The agency’s fact sheet described the sectors it wanted to examine. An investigation of how a product is made or subsidized leaves open which products, if any, may face duties.

The inquiry covers 16 economies, including the EU. The March 17 initiation notice also lists Singapore, Switzerland, Norway, Indonesia, Malaysia, Cambodia, Thailand, South Korea, Vietnam, Taiwan, Bangladesh, Mexico, Japan and India. Hearings ran from May 5 through May 8.

Under Section 304 of the Trade Act, USTR must determine whether the practices are actionable. If it makes an affirmative finding, it must decide what action, if any, to take. The law requires the trade representative to publish the determination and the facts it rests on in the Federal Register.

On July 23, USTR announced final duties on 60 economies after separate investigations into their failures to impose and enforce bans on imports made with forced labor.

On April 9, 2025, President Donald Trump posted that he had authorized a 90-day pause in some higher tariffs while raising the rate for China.

The executive order dated the same day amended the tariff schedule and applied the changes to covered goods entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, at or after 12:01 a.m. Eastern daylight time on April 10.

The reciprocal tariff changes came under different authority from the current investigation.

The written terms tell the company whether its goods fall under the amended tariff schedule and whether its shipment enters before or after the cutoff. The applicable rate can depend on those details and on whether an exemption applies.

After Trump signaled a possible tariff increase on China in October 2025, Bitcoin fell during a broader selloff. That episode shows why a tariff headline can impact crypto investors before importers have any new duties to enter on customs paperwork.

If the USTR determination leads to tariffs, the product coverage, rates, and entry dates will show where costs change and when. Until USTR publishes its findings, the docket remains the place to look for the public decision.

#5027. Jensen Huang’s Wealth Rises $36 Billion as Nvidia Surge Burns Short Sellers for $12 Billion

Jensen Huang’s Wealth Rises $36 Billion as Nvidia Surge Burns Short Sellers for $12 Billion

Jensen Huang’s net worth surged by more than $36 billion on Monday after Nvidia’s board reinstated him as CEO, a dramatic reversal that sent the chipmaker’s stock rocketing and handed its short sellers their worst day in years.

Nvidia shares jumped more than 33% in Monday morning trading, to around $167, recovering the ground lost after Huang resigned 11 days earlier amid a scandal over extramarital affairs, including one with a woman U.S. officials reportedly suspected of spying for China.

The rebound added roughly $36.6 billion to Huang’s fortune, according to Forbes, lifting the co-founder, who owns an estimated 3.5% of Nvidia, to 13th on its global wealth ranking.

You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Nvidia with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.

On the other side of the trade, investors betting against Nvidia were nursing about $12.2 billion in paper losses, their biggest single-day hit since at least 2019, according to data firm ORTEX cited by Reuters.

The reversal wiped out more than $10.5 billion in gains those short sellers had booked just last week. Still, ORTEX noted the bears remain up roughly $14 billion since Oct. 29, and with only about 1% of Nvidia’s float sold short, co-founder Peter Hillerberg characterized the move as a reaction to the news rather than a full short squeeze.

The catalyst was Nvidia’s board voting unanimously to bring Huang back, less than two weeks after his abrupt exit. The return followed President Donald Trump publicly pushing for it, with the president saying the board had sought “assurance on the national security threat” tied to the espionage allegations.

The reinstatement rippled well beyond Nvidia. The news lifted the broader market and dragged crypto up with it, with Bitcoin rallying as risk appetite returned, even as Anthropic shares sank.

The S&P 500 climbed about 5% and the Nasdaq rose nearly 7% on Monday morning, clawing back losses from a Friday selloff driven by anxiety over AI spending.

The episode caps one of the strangest corporate sagas in recent memory: a founder toppled by a spy-tinged scandal, replaced, then restored within days as the president intervened and markets whipsawed on every turn.

For Huang, it marks a remarkable personal recovery, his wealth and his role both snapping back almost overnight.

For Nvidia, whose chips underpin both the AI boom and the data centers increasingly entwined with crypto, the saga is a reminder of how much the market’s fortunes hinge on a single company, and a single person.

#5023. The CFTC opens the door to Bitcoin reserves at US exchanges with a 20% catch

CFTC guidance lets exchanges count Bitcoin toward operating reserves, exposing annual funding buffers to crypto price swings.

On Nov. 23, Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) staff said US futures exchanges and derivatives clearinghouses may count Bitcoin, Ethereum, and qualifying payment stablecoins toward a rolling year of operating costs after applying valuation discounts.

A hypothetical selloff shows how a firm can lose part of that buffer while its liquid assets still cover six months of expenses.

The agency's announcement described the letter as staff guidance. Existing rules remain in force, and the letter offers no assurance that staff would decline to recommend enforcement.

Under the rules for designated contract markets and derivatives clearing organizations, exchanges and clearinghouses need resources to cover at least one year of projected operating costs on a rolling basis.

Within that annual pool, a separate liquidity test calls for enough unencumbered cash or highly liquid securities to cover at least six months of expenses.

The rules allow committed credit lines or similar facilities to make up a liquidity shortfall under certain conditions. The crypto assets in the advisory do not count toward that six-month test.

For the annual calculation, staff says they would raise no objection to the approach in the advisory, which includes a minimum valuation discount of 20% for Bitcoin and Ethereum and a 2% discount for qualifying payment stablecoins.

These discounts, known as haircuts, apply to current market value, so the amount a firm can count moves with the price.

Take a hypothetical exchange with $12 million in annual costs spread evenly across the year, $6 million in unencumbered cash or other eligible liquid assets, and a Bitcoin position worth $7.5 million.

At a fixed 20% haircut, the Bitcoin counts for $6 million. Together, the liquid assets and the discounted Bitcoin position count for $12 million. That matches the annual cost estimate and leaves the exchange with zero headroom.

A 25% drop in the Bitcoin price reduces the position to $5.6 million before the haircut and $4.5 million after. Once the position is valued at the lower price, the firm has $10.5 million in counted resources, $1.5 million below the annual cost estimate.

The $6 million in eligible liquid assets still covers the six-month floor.

Subtract total counted resources of $10.5 million from projected annual costs to obtain the $1.5 million shortfall.

Projected costs and the haircut stay fixed, and the exchange raises no new funds. It starts with zero headroom above projected annual costs.

Staff also flag the risk that operating losses could coincide with falling crypto prices. In that case, a firm's reserve could lose value just as it needs more resources to absorb those losses.

At the stated benchmarks, $1 million worth of Bitcoin or Ethereum counts as $800,000, while $1 million in qualifying payment stablecoins counts as $980,000. The smaller discount for payment stablecoins comes with conditions on which tokens qualify.

Before the GENIUS Act takes effect, staff limit the stablecoin treatment to dollar-denominated tokens from a state-regulated money transmitter or trust company, or a national trust bank.

The issuer must back the tokens with reserves limited to cash, US Treasuries, or overnight Treasury repurchase agreements, held directly or indirectly.

Monthly attestations must cover what the reserves hold and whether their fair value matches the amount in circulation.

Once the law takes effect, the advisory applies its definition and requires a permitted issuer or a foreign issuer that meets the law's applicable conditions.

Customer margin is posted against trading positions, and clearinghouses separately set aside resources to cover clearing-member defaults. The clearinghouse rule bars them from counting the same resources toward both default coverage and operating costs.

The commission registered Backpack Clearing, formerly TLD Clearing Inc., on Nov. 13. Its registration order permits it to clear margined futures as well as fully collateralized futures, options on futures, and swaps.

Those records do not disclose what Backpack Clearing holds for operating costs or whether it uses the staff guidance.

#5021. Base makes quantum security a 2027 priority as regulators warn of risks

Base creator Jesse Pollak says the upcoming Everest upgrade will help prepare wallets for future quantum threats, although further changes will be needed.

Base, an Ethereum layer-2 blockchain developed by Coinbase, is making quantum security a priority for 2027 as it prepares to protect its network against future threats from quantum computers.

Base creator Jesse Pollak told Cointelegraph in an exclusive interview that the upcoming Everest upgrade will introduce a new type of transaction designed to lay the groundwork for quantum-secure wallets.

The network is the second-largest blockchain by decentralized finance (DeFi) total value locked (TVL), with approximately $5.1 billion in assets deposited across its protocols, according to DefiLlama.

The upgrade will not make wallets quantum-resistant right away, but Pollak said it is an early step toward introducing further protections in the future. “That doesn’t mean we’ll be able to solve all of it in 2027, but [it’s] something the team’s going to be working on,” Pollak said.

The plans come as global regulators warn that quantum computers could eventually break the security systems used across financial markets, including blockchain networks.

Quantum computers process information differently from regular computers and could one day allow hackers to access crypto wallets and steal funds. However, many experts have concluded that today’s quantum computers aren’t powerful enough to do this.

One of Base’s first steps will come through Everest, its upcoming fifth network upgrade. Pollak said the upgrade introduces a new transaction type called Base Transactions, which he expects to support future improvements to wallet security.

“That network upgrade doesn’t specifically solve quantum security for these wallets, but it does put in place the framework,” Pollak said.

The current technical specifications for Base Transactions, outlined in EIP-8430, still rely on existing cryptography rather than quantum-resistant signatures. However, the proposed transaction format separates how a transaction is signed from how its signature is verified, allowing the network to introduce new security methods in the future without requiring users to change their wallet addresses.

Base has not set a timeline for introducing quantum-resistant protections, beyond making the work a priority for 2027.

Related: Ethereum dev targets 2028 for quantum resistance, a year early

On Thursday, the International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) warned in a report that sufficiently powerful quantum computers could threaten the security of financial systems.

The international regulator said blockchain networks could be especially difficult to protect because making security changes would require cooperation from many participants. It also warned that these upgrades could create new security problems, raise costs and disrupt transactions.

Meanwhile, advances in artificial intelligence (AI) could make cyberattacks harder to detect and analyze, the report notes.

Governments are also preparing for the threat, with the US National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) introducing its first three security standards designed to protect against quantum attacks in 2024, and releasing further guidance in October 2026. The agency has set 2035 as the primary target for completing the transition to quantum-resistant cryptography across US federal systems.

Beyond quantum security, Pollak outlined four priorities for Base in 2027: expanding trading, payments and lending, while preparing for a future in which AI agents carry out more financial transactions.

Pollak pointed to growing demand for tokenized stocks, saying weekly trading volume on Base had reached $1 billion. He said much of the interest came from investors outside the US seeking easier access to American stocks.

AI agents are also expected to play a bigger role in the network. “Agentic payments was a big trend in 2026. I think that agentic finance is going to be one of the biggest trends of 2027,” he said.

Base’s latest network upgrade, Denim, was rolled out on Nov. 5 and reduced block times from two seconds to 200 milliseconds, allowing the network to produce blocks 10 times faster.

The upgrade was followed by transaction delays on Base. Pollak said Base reviewed the incidents, made fixes and introduced additional testing to help prevent similar problems.

Looking ahead, Pollak said he wants future upgrades to happen without users noticing. “Our goal in 2027 is to make it so that upgrades are non-event. So no one’s even talking about them,” he said.

#5020. UniCredit Opens Bitcoin to Italian Savers, Capping Gains at 65%

UniCredit began selling a six-year, capital-protected certificate linked to BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin ETP to retail clients in Italy, with gains capped at 65%.

UniCredit on Tuesday began selling a capital-protected certificate that lets retail clients in Italy follow the bitcoin price, a product the bank calls the first investment solution of its kind in the country.

The six-year, euro-denominated certificate will be listed on the Munich stock exchange and is linked to the iShares Bitcoin ETP managed by BlackRock, UniCredit said in a release. The placement period runs from Nov. 24 to Dec. 18, 2026.

The note is open only to UniCredit Italia retail clients with specific characteristics, and only through the bank’s advisory service. It can’t be bought independently or by investors who aren’t UniCredit clients, and the minimum investment is €1,000, Italian newswire Teleborsa reported.

A capital-protected certificate is a structured note. The issuing bank promises to repay the original investment at maturity and pays a return tied to an underlying asset, in this case bitcoin through the BlackRock product. Buyers hold a claim on the bank, not bitcoin itself.

If bitcoin is down at maturity, holders get 100% of their capital back. If it rises, they share in the gain up to a maximum return of 65% on the capital invested. Before maturity, the certificate’s price follows market conditions, so the protection applies only at the end of the six years.

That cap works out to roughly 8.7% a year at most, no matter how far bitcoin climbs. And because the certificate is UniCredit’s own debt, the protection depends on the bank’s ability to pay. Documents for a similar UniCredit note in Germany state that no third-party guarantee covers an issuer default.

“With the launch of this certificate, UniCredit is writing a new page of financial innovation in the country, confirming its market leadership,” said Chicco Di Stasi, Head of Group Investment Product Solutions at UniCredit.

“Diversification is no longer just a prudential rule, but the key to capturing the value of the future,” Di Stasi said, adding that the bank is responding to growing client demand and offering the product to Italian savers “for the very first time.”

Di Stasi said the bank is bringing to Italy “a pioneering model already proven by its success in Germany and Austria.” Those earlier notes are denominated in dollars and track BlackRock’s U.S.-listed iShares Bitcoin Trust instead.

HypoVereinsbank, UniCredit’s German unit, sold a version to private clients in March with a 160% cap, or 60% upside. UniCredit Bank Austria launched its own six-year note in April with a 175% cap, or 75% upside. Italy’s 65% falls between the two.

The bank has moved into bitcoin in steps. It first offered a capital-protected bitcoin product to professional clients only in 2025. In May, it placed a bitcoin and ether certificate for professional clients with a €100,000 minimum.

In September, UniCredit was reported to be weighing crypto custody, including the infrastructure to hold and trade digital assets. Elsewhere in Italy, Banca Sella became the first Italian bank licensed for crypto services under MiCA in May.

UniCredit is one of Europe’s largest banks. It reported €918.3 billion in total assets at Sept. 30 and a record €3.3 billion in third-quarter net profit.

Bitcoin traded near $60,400 on Tuesday, more than 50% below its record above $126,000.

#5018. US banks want access to Fed funding on holidays as Wall Street prepares for longer settlement hours

The Fed’s planned payment expansion could allow Bitcoin futures margin to settle on Sundays and weekday holidays.

Thirty-five of 56 domestic banks in a Federal Reserve survey said borrowing from the Fed’s discount window on Sundays and weekday holidays was important, and this has a direct impact on Bitcoin.

The results, released Nov. 20, come as the Fed prepares to add those days to its wholesale payments calendar.

CME’s Thanksgiving advisory shows settlement banks will be closed on Nov. 26, so cash transfers for margin will wait even as CME recalculates its requirements.

The Fed collected responses in September from 91 banks, including 35 foreign banking organizations. In the survey, 24 domestic respondents said matching weekday discount-window hours mattered, and 11 chose access for some hours.

Across all 91 respondents, 41 selected one of those two answers.

The biggest group was unsure whether it would set aside extra cash. In the full sample, 22 expected to temporarily raise reserves ahead of weekends and holidays once the payments schedule expands. Thirty-one did not expect to increase reserves, and 38 were unsure, according to the survey.

In October 2025, the Fed announced it would add Sundays and weekday holidays to Fedwire Funds, its wholesale wire service, and the National Settlement Service. The rollout is expected in 2028 or 2029.

Both services would keep their existing daily hours, and Saturdays would remain outside the business-day schedule.

The Fed’s operating notice treats holiday discount-window loans as a separate decision. The Fed intends to offer eligible banks intraday credit on the added operating days under existing terms.

That credit can bridge a gap between incoming and outgoing payments during the day. Requests for discount-window loans through Discount Window Direct currently follow each local Reserve Bank’s business hours.

CME will recalculate initial margin, the collateral it requires to cover potential losses, at the end of the holiday. It will defer cash margin and collateral transactions, along with settlement variation, the payments that settle gains and losses on open positions.

Under CME’s clearing timetable, trades and transactions submitted for clearing on Thanksgiving will clear Friday. Settlement banks are due to confirm the prior business day’s settlement variation and margin requirements by 7:30 a.m. Central time Friday.

In a 2024 comment letter on the earlier Fedwire proposal, CME said longer wire access could let clearinghouses move dollars for initial margin and settlement variation outside normal banking days. CME called for coordination with settlement banks and other market participants.

For CME Bitcoin futures, an added Fedwire day could let settlement banks that choose to participate move margin dollars on a holiday.

CME would still have to run the applicable clearing and settlement cycle for the margin to settle that day. Banks would have to line up the dollars, and access to holiday discount-window loans depends on the Fed’s lending decision.

#5017. Perps and Swaps: How to Trade the News on Decrypt

Perps and Swaps: How to Trade the News on Decrypt

Readers have traditionally learned about markets in one place and traded them in another. A story about Bitcoin, a public company or a commodity might shape a view, but acting on it meant opening an exchange or a trading app and starting over.

Decrypt set out to close that gap in September 2026, when it announced The Information Exchange: a network that brings together news, data, market prices, probabilities and the ability to trade, around the subjects readers follow.

The Information Exchange sees Decrypt delivering both the reporting and the market infrastructure that links information to trading, while the Solana blockchain provides the network on which trades settle, including token swaps and perpetual futures.

This guide explains what each one is and how to trade it on Decrypt.

Everything on The Information Exchange runs through a Decrypt Money Account, which launched on Solana in October 2026.

A Money Account holds one balance that funds every product on Decrypt: swaps, perpetual futures and prediction markets.The account is self-custodial, meaning Decrypt does not hold users' private keys and cannot act on their behalf. It is designed to work without seed phrases, and network fees are covered, so users don't need to hold SOL, Solana's native token, to pay for transactions.

A swap exchanges one token for another at the current market price. Instead of placing an order on an exchange and waiting for it to fill, the trader sends one token and receives another in a single transaction.

Swaps on Decrypt are powered by Jupiter, a Solana trading platform that offers swaps, lending, borrowing, perpetual futures and portfolio tools. Jupiter finds prices across Solana's trading venues, so users don't need to choose where a trade is executed.

At time of publication, swaps cover a select group of major cryptocurrencies and Solana tokens, as well as tokenized stocks, commodities and other real-world assets.

As of November 2026, the Assets panel of the Portfolio page groups holdings into crypto, stocks, commodities and collectibles, and lists tokens including SOL, BTC, ETH, XRP and HYPE.

Perpetual futures, or perps, are contracts that let traders bet on whether an asset's price will rise or fall without owning the asset. Unlike traditional futures, they have no expiry date. A trader who expects the price to rise goes "long," and one who expects it to fall goes "short."

Perps are usually traded with leverage, which lets a trader control a larger position than their deposit would otherwise allow. Leverage magnifies gains and losses alike, and if the market moves against a position far enough, it can be liquidated, or closed automatically, wiping out the trader's margin.

Perps on Decrypt are powered by Phoenix, a fully onchain perpetuals exchange on Solana developed by Ellipsis Labs—making Decrypt the first media platform to offer perps trading alongside its journalism.

As of November 2026, Phoenix offers more than 100 perps markets on Decrypt, covering crypto, U.S. stocks, gold and pre-IPO companies. Markets trade around the clock, with leverage of up to 40x, according to Phoenix.

Decrypt plans to keep adding products to The Information Exchange, including Situation Rooms: pages that combine breaking news, live data, prices, probabilities and trading around a single subject.

Decrypt operates The Information Exchange, Decrypt Money Accounts and the swaps, perpetual futures and prediction market products described in this guide.

#5015. Researchers find a way to make Bitcoin bridges dramatically cheaper to test

Praxis proposes cheaper proof-based encryption that could help developers build trustless Bitcoin bridges and spending rules.

Praxis, a cryptography preprint cleared for posting on Nov. 23, proposes a way that could make it easier to test Bitcoin payments by reducing both the size of data locked behind a proof and the computing work needed to encrypt it.

Imagine moving Bitcoin through a bridge. The bridge locks the coins on the Bitcoin mainnet while you hold a matching claim on another chain.

To get the Bitcoin back, you would give up that claim. The bridge then needs to release the right amount to the right recipient. A design using witness encryption could make the proof that you gave up the claim unlock the information needed to authorize the payment.

In the Praxis preprint, David Tse, Nikhil Vanjani and Psi Vesely described how to set a condition for opening encrypted information.

In their example, someone with a valid mathematical proof that the condition is met can recover the key that opens the encrypted data. The authors list bridges without a custodian and rules about how Bitcoin can be spent as possible applications.

Bitcoin already checks conditions when someone spends coins. One familiar condition is a valid signature showing that the spender controls the right key. Checking a compact proof of a complicated calculation directly on Bitcoin is harder because its scripting language gives developers a limited set of on-chain checks.

An earlier proposal, Bitcoin PIPEs v2, encrypts a Bitcoin signing key behind a condition. A valid proof unlocks the signing key outside the Bitcoin network, and the resulting transaction carries a signature Bitcoin already knows how to check.

The earlier PIPEs v2 proposal shows where a proof and a signature would each do their work.

A bridge would have to tie the proof and the resulting signing authority to the intended recipient and amount.

In the article’s bridge example, the proof would show that the claim on the other network had been retired.

Illustrative sequence based on PIPEs v2 and Bitcoin's existing signature validation. Praxis is a separate preprint about the underlying type of encryption.

In the article’s bridge example, the proof would show that the claim on the other network had been retired.

In the example, the proof would establish that the matching claim had been retired. Bitcoin would see a signature, so the bridge would have to make sure the signing authority applies to the intended payment, including the recipient and amount.

The encryption scheme lets designers tie access to a proof, and turning that into a working withdrawal system is a separate job.

Earlier BABE research uses witness encryption for one specific kind of mathematical check. Praxis is designed for a much wider range of conditions, as long as a solution to the condition can be checked efficiently.

That opens up more designs researchers could test without asking Bitcoin to do the complicated proof check itself.

In the paper's example, the authors calculate that the encrypted package would take up 7.88 GiB at their stated 100-bit security level.

For the same condition, key length and stated security level, they estimate that the package size and the work of encrypting it are each below one ten-billionth of the costs they calculate for earlier designs by Hair and Sahai.

The authors compared calculated sizes and operation counts across schemes with different security assumptions. Anyone opening the Praxis package would still need access to several gigabytes of encrypted data.

The authors count the work of opening the package from the point when a valid proof is already available. A bridge using this approach would also have to account for the time and computing power needed to produce that proof, wherever it is produced.

The proof system used in the example also needs an honestly run setup. The authors say anyone who kept the setup secret could make proofs that pass the check and open packages tied to that setup.

A team building a bridge would have to handle that risk as well as the logistics of producing proofs and making the encrypted package available when someone needs to withdraw.

#5012. BTCS offloads $44M in ETH to reduce DeFi debt amid market downturn

BTCS sold more than half its Ether holdings to reduce leverage following the market sell-off, while BitMine added another 7,819 ETH to its treasury.

Nasdaq-listed blockchain company BTCS sold approximately 27,300 Ether on Friday to repay $43.8 million in loans on decentralized lending protocol Aave as cryptocurrency markets plunged.

According to a Monday filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, BTCS sold the Ether (ETH) on Nov. 20 and used the proceeds to reduce its outstanding Aave debt to approximately $10.5 million.

The transaction reduced BTCS’s Aave borrowings by approximately 81%, as the company sought to limit liquidation risk amid heightened market volatility. Its remaining Aave positions had a loan-to-value ratio of approximately 32% following the repayment.

BTCS reported approximately $17.9 million in outstanding convertible notes, in addition to its remaining Aave borrowings, according to the company’s announcement. The company also said it temporarily exited liquidity pool positions in its Imperium DeFi business as part of its efforts to reduce exposure to further market volatility.

Following the sale, BTCS held approximately 24,245 ETH, with cash and digital assets valued at a combined $61 million as of Sunday. The 27,300 ETH sale represented approximately 53% of its combined pre-sale ETH holdings.

The move follows a similar reduction in Ether exposure by digital asset manager CoinShares, which disclosed last week that it sold its entire ETH treasury position and half its Solana (SOL) holdings in October to fund share buybacks.

Related: Bitmine edges toward 5% of ETH supply as treasuries report buys amid market slump

Meanwhile, Tom Lee’s BitMine Immersion Technologies continued accumulating Ether, purchasing another 7,819 ETH over the past week despite the market downturn.

According to a Monday announcement, BitMine now holds 6,085,564 ETH, representing 4.98% of the cryptocurrency’s total supply. The company said it has purchased Ether every week since adopting its treasury strategy in June 2025.

BitMine also reported $384 million in cash and marketable securities as of Sunday. The company has staked approximately 5.23 million ETH, representing 86% of its total Ether holdings.

BitMine accounts for roughly 75% of the Ether held in corporate and government treasuries tracked by CoinGecko, which listed 35 entities holding a combined 8.16 million ETH at the time of reporting.

The contrasting strategies come as Ether continues to struggle, trading at approximately $1,743 as of 6:35 p.m. UTC on Monday, down 37.7% over the past year and 24.8% over the past 30 days, according to CoinGecko data.
